pillars.title: Proximity ceiling of the map pack
pillars.section:
## T1 — The Proximity Ceiling of the Map Pack

**Bottom line:** The map pack is a proximity-capped surface. Google ranks it from a business's verified physical address, not its service area ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091); [sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/does-the-service-area-in-google-my-business-impact-ranking/)). One office equals one ranking anchor. Pack visibility decays with distance from that anchor, sharply in the first mile, and collapses fast in dense metros ([rankings.io](https://rankings.io/data-studies/proximity-data-study/)). Organic ranking is materially less proximity-bound — it can rank a city you serve but are not located in ([datapins.com](https://www.datapins.com/seo-for-multiple-cities/); [sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/2025-update-how-proximity-impacts-google-organic-results/)). That asymmetry is the spine: organic is the engine that scales a region; the pack is a near-default proximity prize we still deliver but never center.

**Why the cap exists (mechanism, measured).**
- Google names Distance as one of three core local-ranking factors, alongside Relevance and Prominence ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091)). Proximity is a first-party, structural input — not vendor theory.
- The pack ranks on the verified physical address. The service-area setting is visual only and has no ranking impact ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/does-the-service-area-in-google-my-business-impact-ranking/)). Listing a wide service area does not buy wide pack visibility.
- Google's November 2021 "Vicinity" update — its largest local change since 2017 — increased proximity weight and shrank the pack's radius of visibility, making it harder to rank outside the home city ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/vicinity-algorithm-update/)). The cap is Google-imposed, not an artifact of weak SEO.

**How fast it decays (measured, n≈1,100 across 50 cities).**
- Pack rank follows exponential decay with a sharp first-mile cliff — an average drop of ~8 positions in the first mile ([rankings.io](https://rankings.io/data-studies/proximity-data-study/)).
- The effective radius is not a universal mile number. Top-20 exit rates by the edge of a 10-mile grid range from ~27% (Pittsburgh) to ~92% (Queens); dense metros sit ~80%+ (Boston 81.5%, LA 82.3%, NYC 80.8%) ([rankings.io](https://rankings.io/data-studies/proximity-data-study/)). This is why we promise a **floor**, not a fixed radius.

**What scaling the pack actually requires.**
- Reach is anchored to a point, so extending pack coverage to a region means adding staffed physical locations — one proximity bubble each ([brandonrollins.com](https://brandonrollins.com/p/how-to-rank-a-service-area-business-in-google)). The pack scales by capex/footprint. Concede this precisely: the cap is **per-location**, not company-wide. One office = one bubble.

**Why organic escapes it.**
- Google's organic algorithm is less proximity-constrained than Maps; organic city pages can rank in a city a business services but is not located in ([datapins.com](https://www.datapins.com/seo-for-multiple-cities/)). Sterling Sky's longitudinal study finds proximity is "less influential than in the past" on organic, and the pack is the more proximity-bound surface ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/2025-update-how-proximity-impacts-google-organic-results/)).
- Scaling organic = content, on-page, authority — far cheaper per market than opening offices. That cost asymmetry is the offer argument.

**Where the pack still earns its keep.**
- The pack captures a large but **not dominant** share of clicks: ~29-32% pack vs ~44-51% organic in a controlled 5,500-tester study — organic out-clicks the pack ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-services-ads-click-study/)). The pack is the highest-intent surface within radius, valuable for the home market and the emergency slice. Never call it useless.

**What NOT to oversell:** Do not assert a fixed "X-mile" radius, a precise proximity-weight percentage, or a hard company-wide revenue cap — the radius is density-dependent and directional, the weight is disputed and likely declining, and the per-location cap can be lifted with capex.

loadBearing.claim: The map pack ranks from a business's verified physical address, not its listed service area — the service-area setting is visual only and has no ranking impact. This anchors each office's pack reach to one geographic point.
loadBearing.stat: service-area setting has zero ranking impact; rankings based on verified address
loadBearing.snippet: the ranking is based on the address at which the business verified the listing. The only impact that the service area has is visual.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the structural root of the per-location cap and the entire 'pack is proximity-bound, organic is not' offer spine. If this falls, the cap thesis falls.
loadBearing.measured_or_modeled: measured (case study); corroborated by Google first-party docs (support.google.com/business/answer/7091)

loadBearing.claim: Google's November 2021 'Vicinity' update — its largest local algorithm change since 2017 — increased proximity weight and shrank the pack's radius of visibility, making it harder for one location to rank in the 3-pack outside its home city.
loadBearing.stat: rolled out Nov 30–Dec 8, 2021; biggest local update since 2017; radius of visibility reduced
loadBearing.snippet: The update heavily increased the weight of proximity ... 'shrunk' the size of the map pack, making it much harder for businesses to rank in the 3-pack for locations outside their home city.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Keystone corroborator that the radius cap is Google-imposed by design, not a symptom of weak SEO. Defends the offer against 'just optimize harder and you'll rank everywhere.'
loadBearing.measured_or_modeled: measured (confirmed algorithm update + observed ranking shifts)

loadBearing.claim: Pack ranking decays exponentially with distance from the anchor, with a sharp first-mile cliff averaging ~8 positions dropped in the first mile across ~1,100 firms sampled in 50 cities.
loadBearing.stat: exponential decay (lambda≈2.3); ~-8 positions in the first mile; n≈1,100 across 50 cities; 15x15 grid at 10mi
loadBearing.snippet: the ranking drops dramatically in the first mile in all cities. On average, the drop in ranking in the first mile is -8 positions ... follows an exponential decay rule (decay constant lambda of 2.3 across all cities).
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The measured radius-decay mechanism behind the effective ceiling — the quantitative spine. Label as measured/directional on the precise mileage; do not convert lambda into a fixed mile promise.
loadBearing.measured_or_modeled: measured (geo-grid study); radius-to-miles is directional, density-dependent

loadBearing.claim: The pack captures a large but not dominant share of local clicks — organic out-clicks the pack (~44-51% organic vs ~29-32% pack) in a controlled 5,500-tester study.
loadBearing.stat: pack 28.8% (LSAs present) / 32.3% (absent); organic 43.9% / 50.8%; n=5,500
loadBearing.snippet: Local Pack 28.8% of clicks; Organic Results 43.9%; when LSAs absent organic 50.8% vs Local Pack 32.3%. Study: 5,500 testers across five SAB categories in San Francisco.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Empirical basis for 'organic is the engine, pack is a byproduct' and corrects the inflated '60-90% pack' myth. Reel/slide-bound; FTC-exposed if overstated. Single-metro study — present as directional on exact splits.

loadBearing.claim: Google's organic algorithm is materially less proximity-constrained than Maps, so organic pages can rank in a city the business services but is not physically located in; the pack is the more proximity-bound surface.
loadBearing.stat: qualitative structural distinction; Sterling Sky 2025: proximity 'less influential than in the past' on organic
loadBearing.snippet: Sterling Sky longitudinal study (2022 vs 2025): proximity is less influential than in the past on organic results; in 2022 proximity had a stronger impact on localized-organic than on the Local Pack.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The structural keystone of the offer: organic is the mechanism that escapes the proximity cap; the pack cannot. Without this, 'build the authority site to scale the region' loses its causal basis.
loadBearing.measured_or_modeled: measured (longitudinal listing study) + directional (datapins corroboration at datapins.com/seo-for-multiple-cities)

whatNotToOversell: Do not state a fixed 'X-mile' effective radius — it is density-dependent (27% to 92% top-20 exit across metros) and directional, not a measured constant. Promise a floor, project a ceiling.

Do not assert a single precise proximity-weight percentage (e.g. '55%'). The weight is from expert surveys (modeled/perceived), is disputed, and is likely declining; some 2025 sources put it near 15%. State the mechanism, not a number.

Do not claim a hard company-wide revenue cap. The cap is per-LOCATION; it can be lifted with capex (new staffed offices, each a new proximity bubble). The argument is cost asymmetry, not impossibility.

Do not call the pack useless or a pure non-scaling byproduct — it still takes ~29-44% of clicks and is the highest-intent surface within radius, especially for the home market and emergency slice. We win it on ties.
Do not claim prominence/proximity coefficients from Google — Distance/Relevance/Prominence are named as factors, but no causal weights are published. Cite the factor, not a coefficient.
Do not present single-metro or single-vertical studies (BrightLocal SF testers; Rankings.io law-firm keyword) as universal — label scope; they are directional outside their sample.
Exclude any PBN / link-scheme / gray-hat path entirely; ongoing client-managed off-page is out of scope and must not be used to back-fill the radius-escape claim.
gaps: No primary source publishes a single defensible universal effective radius in miles; the ~5-7mi figure remains a directional synthesis of exponential-decay + density-variance data, not a measured constant. Treat as modeled.

No source quantifies a per-location DOLLAR revenue cap for pack-sourced leads; the cap is a sound logical inference (address-anchored ranking + finite within-radius population + 3 shared slots), not a measured figure — must be labeled as derived.
The proximity weight is directional (expert-survey/perceived), never a published causal % — the warm-context caution against asserting '55%' holds; no primary Whitespark table gives a clean number.

Roofing-specific decay data is thin: the cleanest per-mile decay study (rankings.io, -8 positions/mile) is a LAW-FIRM dataset. Mechanism (address-anchored proximity) is industry-agnostic, but a roofing-specific geo-grid would harden the claim — consider a Local Falcon SoLV roofing scan as own-data proof.
Exact post-Vicinity radius shrink is described qualitatively ('shrunk the pack', 'harder outside home city') but not given as a before/after mile delta in any primary source.

No PRIMARY (Google first-party) numeric statement of an effective pack radius exists — Google documents Distance qualitatively only; every mile figure (1-2mi near-me, 5-10mi max, 30-50mi crew radius) is third-party/modeled. The ~5-7mi 'effective ceiling' remains a defensible MODELED midpoint, not a Google-published number. Promise the floor, label the ceiling modeled.

The precise WEIGHT of proximity is genuinely unresolved across credible sources (cited at ~15% AND ~55% in 2025-2026). This pillar should stop trying to nail a single percentage and instead lean on the measured DECAY mechanism + the non-controllability point, both of which are robust.

No NC/Triangle-specific or roofing-specific quantified proximity-decay dataset was found (the strongest measured decay study is the personal-injury-lawyer vertical). A roofing/NC geo-grid SoLV study would be the ideal first-party proof asset to commission rather than cite.

No clean, independent dollar-figure study ties 'pack-sourced lead ceiling' to a specific single-location revenue cap (e.g., '$X/yr max from one GBP'). The $5-10M-needs-footprint logic is assembled from pricing tiers + the address-anchored mechanism, not a single measured source — keep it as a reasoned argument, not a cited statistic.

The BrightLocal Local Services Ads click study (round 1 spine, 29-32% pack vs 44-51% organic) is the single best click-share source but is one study, one query set — a second independent controlled click-share study would harden it against the widely-cited 44%/68% pack-dominant myth.

counter.point: Individual-firm variance is large: 'Every law firm behaves differently. Some hold rankings for several miles, others drop out of the top 20 almost immediately.' A strong-SEO, high-prominence business can stretch its effective radius meaningfully beyond a weak one.
counter.soWhat: KM cannot promise a fixed mile number, but this actually SUPPORTS the offer: organic prominence (links, reviews, on-page) is exactly what dilates the radius — so the lever KM sells (organic dominance) is the same lever that buys extra pack reach. Promise the floor, project the ceiling.

counter.point: The pack still captures ~29-44% of local clicks and is the highest-intent surface within radius — calling it a non-scaling 'byproduct' risks underselling a genuinely valuable lead source for the home-market and emergency slice.
counter.soWhat: Frame the pack as the near-default proximity prize KM still delivers (and wins on ties), while organic regional dominance is the engine that scales past one office. Never say 'useless.'

counter.point: Multi-location is the sanctioned scaling path: real, staffed offices each create a new proximity bubble, and the biggest competitors already do this. A roofer COULD scale pack coverage by opening offices — pack isn't inherently capped at the company level, only at the per-location level.
counter.soWhat: Concede the per-LOCATION framing precisely: one office = capped. Scaling the pack requires capex (new staffed addresses); scaling organic requires content/links/authority — far cheaper per market. That cost asymmetry is the offer argument, not a claim that pack can never grow.

counter.point: No source publishes a single defensible 'X mile' radius or a per-location dollar revenue cap; the radius is density-dependent and the revenue cap is a logical inference, not a measured constant.
counter.soWhat: Label the ~5-7mi figure as directional/modeled and the revenue cap as a derived inference from address-anchored ranking + density-variable decay — never as a measured universal number. This keeps the FTC-exposed offer claim defensible.

counter.point: The 'proximity is the dominant / top-weighted local factor' framing is contested and possibly trending DOWN. Sterling Sky's 2025 study finds proximity 'less influential than in the past' on organic; multiple 2025 sources cite proximity at only ~15% of ranking weight (down from 25-30% in 2020), while Whitespark's survey is read elsewhere at ~55%. The honest position: proximity is a structurally heavy, NON-controllable input on the PACK whose precise weight is disputed and likely declining — do not assert a single high percentage.
counter.soWhat: Promise the FLOOR and the mechanism (address-anchored pack decay), not a precise proximity-weight number. The declining-weight finding actually STRENGTHENS the offer: it means prominence/authority (organic, which we build) increasingly overcomes distance.

counter.point: Prominence/authority can OVERCOME proximity — Search Engine Land and others note a business can rank beyond its immediate radius when entity strength, review volume, and local backlinks outweigh distance; Search Engine Land explicitly frames overcoming proximity bias WITHOUT adding physical locations. This partially undercuts a hard 'one office = a hard cap' claim.
counter.soWhat: Reframe, do not retreat: this is the offer's own thesis — authority (organic) beats proximity. The cap is on the PACK absent authority; the escape route is exactly the deep authority site King Maker builds. Keep the cap claim scoped to the pack for an UN-optimized listing.

counter.point: The inflated 'pack dominates clicks' myth is alive and widely cited: sources claim the map pack gets ~44% of clicks and that '68% prefer the 3-pack vs 27% organic' — directly contradicting round 1's controlled BrightLocal study (29-32% pack vs 44-51% organic). A skeptic will quote the pack-dominant figures.
counter.soWhat: Anchor the click-share claim ONLY on the controlled 5,500-tester BrightLocal study and explicitly name the 44%/68% figures as the un-sourced or self-reported-survey myth they correct. Do not let an opponent's stat go unrebutted in the reel/pitch.

counter.point: A commonly recommended 'fix' for the proximity cap is opening a satellite/co-working address in a target city to plant a new proximity bubble. This is a footprint-scaling tactic but, when the address is not a genuine staffed location, it is a Google-guidelines violation (fake-location / lead-gen spam) and a suspension risk.
counter.soWhat: EXCLUDE per the no-gray-hat rule. Use it as a contrast point: the pack tempts contractors into address-gaming to scale; the defensible path is organic authority. Never recommend co-working/virtual addresses to extend pack reach.

allClaims.claim: Google itself names Distance (proximity of each business to the searcher) as one of three primary local-ranking factors, alongside Relevance and Prominence — confirming proximity is a structural, first-party input to the pack, not a vendor theory.
allClaims.stat: 1 of 3 core factors (Relevance, Distance, Prominence)
allClaims.snippet: Distance: 'how far each business is from the customer who's searching' ... Prominence: 'how well-known a business is ... based on info like how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have.'

allClaims.claim: Proximity is the single most heavily weighted local-PACK factor in the expert-survey consensus — the top finder/pack factor. (Flag: expert-survey = modeled/perceived weight, not a published causal coefficient; do not assert a precise '55%'.)
allClaims.stat: ranked #1 pack factor (directional, no defensible %)
allClaims.snippet: Moz/Whitespark surveys: 'Proximity of Address to the Point of Search' is the most important factor to survey participants for the Local Pack; proximity to where the user searches from increased in importance.

allClaims.claim: Google's November 2021 'Vicinity' update — its largest local algorithm change in ~5 years — explicitly increased proximity weight and SHRANK the pack's radius of visibility, making it much harder for one location to rank in the 3-pack outside its home city. This is the keystone corroborator that the radius is a Google-imposed cap, not an artifact of weak SEO.
allClaims.stat: rolled out Nov 30–Dec 8, 2021; biggest local update since 2017
allClaims.snippet: The update heavily increased the weight of proximity ... 'shrunk' the size of the map pack, making it much harder for businesses to rank in the 3-pack for locations outside their home city; businesses that previously ranked across multiple cities saw visibility reduced outside their immediate area.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: measured (confirmed algorithm update + observed ranking shifts)

allClaims.claim: Pack rankings decay with distance following EXPONENTIAL decay with a sharp first-mile cliff: across 1,100 samples the average drop was -8 positions per mile, with the immediate first-mile drop ranging 5.3 to 11.8 positions. This is the measured radius-decay mechanism behind the ~5-7mi effective ceiling.
allClaims.stat: -8 positions/mile avg; 5.3–11.8 position first-mile drop; n=1,100
allClaims.snippet: 'immediately dropping anywhere from 5.3 to 11.8 positions' ... 'For all 1100 samples, the average drop was -8 positions.' ... 'rankings follow the law of exponential decay'

allClaims.claim: The effective radius is NOT a universal mile number — it varies sharply with population/competition density. In dense metros a single location falls out of the top 20 almost immediately; in lower-density metros it holds far longer. This is why KM must promise a FLOOR, not a fixed radius.
allClaims.stat: dense: Boston 81.5% / LA 82.3% / NYC 80.8% dropped from top 20; sparse: Columbus 28.5% / Pittsburgh 26.7%
allClaims.snippet: 'In Boston (81.5%), Los Angeles (82.3%), and New York City (80.8%), nearly every law firm has dropped out of the top 20' ... 'In cities like Columbus (28.5%) and Pittsburgh (26.7%), less than a third of firms had dropped out'

allClaims.claim: Pack ranking is computed from the VERIFIED PHYSICAL ADDRESS, not the listed service area — so a single office's pack reach is anchored to one geographic point. The service-area setting is visual only and does not extend rankings. This is the structural root of the per-location revenue cap.
allClaims.stat: service-area setting has zero ranking impact
allClaims.snippet: 'the ranking is based on the address at which the business verified the listing. The only impact that the service area has is visual.' ... 'Rankings are based on the address used to verify the listing.'

allClaims.claim: Because reach is anchored to a physical point, scaling pack coverage to a region requires ADDING physical locations (one proximity bubble each) — confirming the pack scales by capex/footprint, not by site depth. One office = one bubble = a hard revenue cap on pack-sourced leads.
allClaims.stat: each staffed physical address = one new proximity bubble; up to 20 service areas allowed but they don't rank
allClaims.snippet: 'Proximity to the searcher is the single strongest ranking signal in Google Maps' ... 'multiple Google Business Profile locations — each with a legitimate physical address, staffed and operational — each create their own ranking proximity bubble.'

allClaims.claim: The pack captures a large but NOT dominant share of local clicks — ~29-32% pack vs ~44-51% organic in a controlled 5,500-tester study. Organic OUT-CLICKS the pack. This is the empirical spine of KM's 'organic is the engine, pack is a byproduct' offer frame; corrects the inflated '60-90% pack' myth.
allClaims.stat: pack 28.8% (LSAs present) / 32.3% (absent); organic 43.9% / 50.8%; n=5,500
allClaims.snippet: Local Pack '28.8%' of clicks; Organic Results '43.9%'; when LSAs absent organic '50.8%' vs Local Pack '32.3%'. Study: '5,500 testers' across five SAB categories in San Francisco.

allClaims.claim: Google recommends a service area no larger than roughly a 2-hour drive — but that is a guideline ceiling on the SETTING, not a ranking radius. Combined with the address-anchored ranking finding, it underscores that listing a wide area does not buy wide pack visibility.
allClaims.stat: Google guidance: service area within ~2-hour drive of base
allClaims.snippet: 'Google recommends that your service area not extend much beyond a two hour drive from your business's physical base. However, the ranking is based on the address at which the business verified the listing, not the service area itself.'

allClaims.claim: A visible physical address is itself a measured top-10 pack factor (7th most influential, across 8,186 businesses / 200 cities) — independent confirmation that the pack rewards a real, located office and structurally disadvantages address-hiding service businesses. Reinforces that the pack is location-bound, not site-depth-bound.
allClaims.stat: visible address = 7th most influential pack factor; n=8,186 businesses / 200 cities
allClaims.snippet: Study of 8,186 businesses across 200 cities: 'a negative correlation between hiding your address and ranking well in the local pack' — 'Have a real office with a real address.' Visible address ranks as the 7th most influential factor.

allClaims.claim: Within the pack, click share is nearly flat across the three slots (#1 ~17.8%, #2 ~15.4%, #3 ~15.1%) — so the pack is the highest-intent surface WITHIN radius, but its total click pool is capped and shared three ways. The pack is valuable, not useless; it is just bounded.
allClaims.snippet: 'The #1 local pack result received 17.8% of click-throughs, followed by 15.4% for #2 and 15.1% for #3.' Pack ~44% of clicks vs organic ~29% in their aggregate framing.

allClaims.claim: Whitespark attributes a 360% jump in the importance of proximity-to-centroid directly to the post-Vicinity radius reduction — tying the modeled survey weight to the measured 2021 algorithm change, and confirming the radius tightened by Google design.
allClaims.stat: +360% signal-importance increase for proximity-to-centroid post-Vicinity
allClaims.snippet: 'Proximity of address to centroid ... saw signal importance increase 360% since the last LSRF, likely due to the reduction in the radius of visibility after the Vicinity update in late 2021.'
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: modeled (expert survey, tied to measured update)

allClaims.claim: The measured pack-radius decay follows an exponential-decay law with an estimated decay constant (lambda) of 2.3 across all cities, with the average drop in the FIRST MILE being -8 ranking positions — quantifying the sharp first-mile cliff that creates the effective ceiling. (Same Rankings.io study cited in round 1, but this captures the exponential model + decay constant as a stronger, more precise statement of the mechanism.)
allClaims.stat: exponential decay, lambda=2.3; first-mile drop = -8 positions; ~1,100 firms sampled across 50 cities; 15x15 grid (225 points) at 10mi radius; keyword 'car accident lawyer'
allClaims.snippet: the ranking drops dramatically in the first mile; in all cities. On average, the drop in ranking in the first mile is -8 positions ... the drop in the ranking follows an exponential decay rule (decay constant lambda of 2.3 across all cities).

allClaims.claim: The share of businesses that fall out of the top 20 by the edge of the proximity radius ranges from 27% (Pittsburgh) to 92% (Queens) — a measured, city-level confirmation that the effective radius is NOT a universal mile figure but collapses fast in dense/competitive metros and holds far longer in low-density ones. This is the empirical basis for promising a FLOOR not a fixed radius.
allClaims.stat: top-20 exit rate ranges 27% (Pittsburgh) to 92% (Queens); dense metros ~80%+ (Boston 81.5%, LA 82.3%, NYC 80.8%)
allClaims.snippet: the percentage of firms dropping from top 20 rankings ranges from 27% in Pittsburgh to 92% in Queens ... Some top-ranking firms do not even see a dip in the 10-mile radius, while some law firms drop very quickly out of the top 20.

allClaims.claim: Google's ORGANIC algorithm is materially less proximity-constrained than the Maps/pack algorithm, so organic city pages can rank in a city the business SERVICES but is NOT physically located in — whereas the pack favors the locally-addressed listing. This is the structural keystone of the offer spine: organic is the mechanism that escapes the proximity cap; the pack cannot.
allClaims.stat: qualitative structural distinction (pack = address-anchored; organic = content/authority-anchored)
allClaims.snippet: Google's organic algorithm (the traditional ten blue links) is less constraining than its Google Maps counterpart, providing a better opportunity for SABs to rank ... [organic city pages can rank] in a city that your business has serviced but is not actually located in.

allClaims.claim: Sterling Sky's own longitudinal listing study (2022 vs 2025) found proximity 'is less influential than in the past' on ORGANIC results, and that in their 2022 study proximity had a STRONGER impact on localized-organic than on the Local Pack — i.e., the pack is the MORE proximity-bound surface, and organic is comparatively escapable. Independent first-party corroboration of the spine, and honest counter-evidence to any 'proximity is rising everywhere' overclaim.
allClaims.stat: directional, longitudinal (2022 vs 2025); proximity influence on organic declining
allClaims.snippet: Proximity still affects organic rankings, but is less influential than in the past ... proximity was still a factor, but it didn't seem to have as strong an influence on organic rankings as it did in the 2022 study ... proximity had a stronger impact on rankings in the localized organic results than in the Local Pack results [2022].

allClaims.claim: Proximity is structurally NOT optimizable: per BrightLocal's local-algorithm guide, 'there isn't much a business can do to target this pillar' beyond accurate NAP. This is the load-bearing honesty point behind the offer — you cannot SEO your way past the proximity cap on the pack, which is precisely why organic (which you CAN build) is the regional-dominance engine.
allClaims.stat: qualitative; proximity = non-controllable pillar
allClaims.snippet: There isn't much a business can do to target this pillar. However, making sure that your Google Business Profile and other listings have an accurate Name, Address, and Phone Number (NAP) is a good start.

allClaims.claim: In the roofing vertical specifically, Google evaluates proximity/relevance/prominence SEPARATELY for each local market, so a single office only surfaces in the pack near that office — 'a searcher in the northern suburbs will see different roofing companies than someone in the southern part of the SAME city.' Reaching cities beyond the office is done via organic city-specific service pages, not the pack. Roofing-vertical confirmation of both the per-location cap and the organic-reach mechanism.
allClaims.stat: per-market evaluation; recommended realistic crew radius 30-50 miles or named cities
allClaims.snippet: A searcher in the northern suburbs will see different roofing companies than someone in the southern part of the same city ... Each location is a separate local market with different competitors, proximity signals, and demand ... Google evaluates proximity, relevance, and prominence separately for each local market ... Limit radius to 30-50 miles or list specific cities served.

allClaims.claim: Roofing carries a long, multi-search sales cycle, so a deep organic presence (repeat trust-building visits over days) compounds in a way the single-tap pack does not — the vertical-specific reason organic is the engine for high-ticket roofing, beyond raw click share. Supports centering organic over the pack for THIS vertical specifically.
allClaims.stat: qualitative; longer sales cycle = compounding organic value
allClaims.snippet: services with longer sales cycles, such as roofing, benefit significantly from a strong organic presence because the potential customer may search multiple times over several days before making a decision, and each time they find your content and your site, trust builds.

allClaims.claim: Industry pricing tiers confirm regional/state scale ($5-10M-class market capture) is bought with footprint + heavy ongoing budget, not pack optimization: local 1-2 city = $4.5-7.5k/mo, regional multi-city/state = $7.5-20k/mo, national/enterprise = $20-60k+/mo, and each new physical location 'strengthens domain authority' (organic), positioning the firm as a regional/national player. Confirms the pack scales by capex/footprint while ORGANIC domain authority is the compounding regional engine.
allClaims.stat: regional multi-state SEO = $7.5k-20k/mo; national/enterprise = $20k-60k+/mo; lead lift 100-300% with optimization
allClaims.snippet: each new location strengthening domain authority, expanding content opportunities, and positioning your roofing company as a regional or national player ... regional contractors (multi-city/state) $7,500-$20,000/mo, and national/enterprise roofing groups $20,000-$60,000+/mo.

allClaims.claim: Google itself removed proximity-to-searcher as a top Local Services Ads ranking factor as of April 2025, shifting LSA ranking from 'who's closest' to 'who performs best' — evidence that even Google treats raw proximity as a blunt, undesirable ranking input on surfaces it can re-engineer. Corroborates that proximity is a structural cap, not a quality signal a contractor should build a strategy around.
allClaims.stat: April 2025 LSA change; proximity removed as top LSA factor
allClaims.snippet: As of April 2025, proximity to the searcher is no longer a top-ranking factor in determining which LSAs appear at the top of the page, shifting the spotlight from 'who's closest' to 'who performs best.'

pillars.title: Prominence dilates the pack radius (organic feeds the map)
pillars.section:
## T2 — Prominence dilates the pack radius (organic feeds the map)

**Bottom line: web authority is a stated, first-party input to local-pack ranking — but it widens the effective radius, it does not remove the distance cap. We sell the engine (organic dominance) and deliver the byproduct (a proximity-capped pack lift). We never sell the site as the pack-winner.**

Google names three local ranking factors: relevance, distance, and prominence ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en)). Prominence is defined first-party as "how well-known a business is," and Google states it is "based on info like how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have" ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en)). So organic web authority is not a theory we invented — it is a ranking input Google publishes itself.

The mechanism is radius dilation. A business with stronger prominence and relevance signals than physically-closer competitors can outrank them and rank across a wider geographic radius ([searchengineland.com](https://searchengineland.com/guide/google-proximity-bias-in-local-search)). Practitioners call this "ranking radius" — a well-optimized site plus strong reputation lets a business compete farther from its physical address ([bigorangeplanet.com](https://www.bigorangeplanet.com/2026/05/17/how-proximity-impacts-local-rankings-in-google-search)). This is directional and mechanistic. There is no defensible miles-per-link figure — anyone quoting one is making it up.

The payoff is asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the whole offer. Web/link authority moves ORGANIC rankings strongly and the LOCAL PACK only weakly. The 2026 Whitespark Local Search Ranking Factors survey (47 experts, modeled weights) puts on-page signals near 33% in local organic versus ~15% in the local pack — roughly 2x heavier organically — with links a top-tier organic factor (~24%) but a minor pack one ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/local-search-ranking-factors/)). BrightLocal's read of the same data: link signals keep dropping, "particularly for local pack rankings" (~8% category weight) ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/google-local-algorithm-and-ranking-factors/)). Because Whitespark is an expert-opinion survey (modeled, not measured), we corroborate it with measured field work: Joy Hawkins / Sterling Sky isolated link building and showed organic and pack rankings respond very differently — "links do not impact the organic + local algorithm the same" ([brightonseo.com](https://brightonseo.com/events/san-diego-2024/talks/does-link-building-actually-influence-local-pack-rankings)).

So the floor we promise and the ceiling we project:
- **Floor (defensible, always true):** organic authority is a published prominence input; building it widens the site's organic reach and supports the pack. Organic and local are independent surfaces — the site can own page-one organic outright while the pack is contested ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/google-local-algorithm-and-ranking-factors/)).
- **Ceiling (directional, never a point-promise):** a more prominent business slightly farther out can outrank a closer competitor with weak signals ([searchengineland.com](https://searchengineland.com/guide/google-proximity-bias-in-local-search)) — which is exactly how organic dominance scales a brand past the ~5-mile pack radius that caps local revenue.

The hard counterweight, stated plainly: proximity still gates the pack. The best independent measurement of pack drivers (Sterling Sky, 8,186 businesses across 200 cities) found on-page content correlates only SLIGHTLY with pack ranking — review recency and a visible address dominated ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/what-gets-you-ranking-for-near-me-2025/)). Pack results cluster in a tight several-mile radius even in huge metros ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/local-pack-clustering-making-sense-of-googles-ranking-patterns/)), and hiding the address — removing the proximity anchor — tanked a real client's rankings and erased the pack for a keyword entirely ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/hiding-address-google-business-ranking/)). Distance is a structural input the site cannot override. Prominence dilates the radius around a REAL office; it does not let a business rank anywhere regardless of location.

**What NOT to oversell:** never promise a measured radius gain, a prominence-beats-proximity percentage (the 60%/15% split is uncited agency lore), or that organic ranking "lifts pack rank by X" — the organic↔local correlation is marketer belief, not algorithmic causation. The site wins organic and supports the pack; proximity + review velocity win the pack, and we deliver those off-page, not with pages.

loadBearing.claim: Google's own first-party definition of the local-pack Prominence ranking factor explicitly counts inbound website links and reviews as inputs — making web/organic authority a stated Google local-ranking factor.
loadBearing.stat: Prominence is 1 of 3 named ranking factors (relevance, distance, prominence); inputs named verbatim: 'how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have.'
loadBearing.snippet: Prominence means how well-known a business is. Prominent places are more likely to show up in search results. This factor's also based on info like how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have. More reviews and positive ratings can help your business's local ranking.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the FOUNDATION of the offer and the only first-party source. It converts 'organic feeds the pack' from agency theory into a Google-published fact — FTC-defensible. Re-verified verbatim at gather time via WebFetch.
loadBearing.measured_or_modeled: directional (Google first-party definition; named input, not a measured weight)

loadBearing.claim: A more prominent/authoritative business can outrank physically-closer competitors and rank across a WIDER geographic radius — the radius-dilation mechanism, stated mechanistically, not as a measured miles-per-link figure.
loadBearing.stat: No numeric radius; directional — specialized/authoritative businesses 'rank across a wider radius' and 'a business slightly farther away but significantly more prominent and relevant can still outrank a closer competitor.'
loadBearing.snippet: If your business has built up stronger signals of relevance and prominence than competitors who are physically nearer to a searcher, you may succeed at outranking them. ... a business that is slightly farther away but significantly more prominent and relevant can still outrank a closer competitor.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the literal 'prominence dilates the radius' mechanism the pillar is named for. Independent trade source (Search Engine Land), not a vendor with skin in the game. Pair it with the floor/ceiling framing so it stays directional.

loadBearing.claim: The 2026 Whitespark Local Search Ranking Factors survey quantifies the asymmetry: on-page/website signals are weighted ~2x more in Local Organic than in the Local Pack, and links are a top-tier organic factor but minor for the pack.
loadBearing.stat: Local Pack: GBP ~32%, on-page ~15%. Local Organic: on-page ~33%, links ~24%. On-page ~2x heavier organically (47 experts, 187 factors, published Nov 6 2025).
loadBearing.snippet: Local Pack (Map results) weights GBP signals at 32% and on-page at 15%. Local organic (standard results) weights on-page at 33% and links at 24%.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The strongest quantification that the site WINS organic and only SUPPORTS the pack — the core of KM's organic-first emphasis. MUST be labeled modeled/surveyed (expert opinion, not measured) and paired with the measured Sterling Sky link-isolation case studies, or a skeptic dismisses it as crowdsourced perception.

loadBearing.claim: Named-authority MEASURED case studies (Joy Hawkins / Sterling Sky) that isolated link building show organic and local-pack rankings respond very differently — establishing the asymmetry causally, not by survey opinion.
loadBearing.stat: BrightonSEO San Diego 2024 talk: case studies where 'we did nothing but link building' produced 'very different' organic vs local results; 'Links do not impact the organic + local algorithm the same.'
loadBearing.snippet: In this talk, Joy will share never-before-seen case studies that show exactly what happened to both organic and local rankings when we did nothing but link building. Spoiler alert: the results were very different. Links do not impact the organic + local algorithm the same.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The measured corroborator that rescues T2-3 from being opinion-only. It is the cleanest evidence that web/link authority feeds organic far more than the pack — the spine of the offer. Cite as the measured backstop under the modeled Whitespark weights.

loadBearing.claim: Proximity still gates the pack — the mandatory not-oversell counterweight. The best independent measurement found on-page content correlates only slightly with pack rank, results cluster in a tight radius, and removing the address anchor erases the pack.
loadBearing.stat: Sterling Sky: 8,186 businesses / 200 cities; on-page content has only a 'slight correlation' with pack rank; review recency + visible address dominate; hiding the address tanked rankings and made the pack disappear for a keyword.
loadBearing.snippet: There is a slight correlation between having more substantive words on your page and better local rankings. ... The number of reviews you've gotten this month matters more than your total number of reviews. ... a negative correlation between hiding your address and ranking well in the local pack.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the honesty ceiling that keeps the whole pillar FTC-defensible. It is why we promise a FLOOR (organic supports prominence) and never a measured radius gain. On a slide it is the 'distance still caps the pack' counterweight that earns the audience's trust in everything else.

whatNotToOversell: Never promise a measured radius gain or a miles-per-link figure — radius dilation is directional/mechanistic; no source quantifies it in distance.

Do not use the '60% prominence / 15% proximity' split — it is uncited agency lore. The only defensible quantification is the Whitespark on-page asymmetry (~33% organic vs ~15% pack), and that is modeled/surveyed, not measured.
Do not claim organic ranking 'lifts pack rank by X.' The 88% organic-local correlation is marketer BELIEF (survey), not algorithmic causation — keep it at 'organic feeds a stated prominence input.'

Do not sell the site as the pack-winner. Proximity gates the pack (tight several-mile cluster; hiding the address erases it); review recency + visible address are the dominant pack levers, and those are off-page fulfillment, not pages.
Label Whitespark weights 'modeled/surveyed' and always pair them with the measured Sterling Sky link-isolation case studies, or a skeptic dismisses the asymmetry as crowdsourced opinion.

Do not assert organic-first is universal best practice — most local-SEO guidance prioritizes the pack for small local businesses. KM's organic-first emphasis rests specifically on the high-ticket/regional-scale argument (only organic scales past the ~5-mile pack radius), not on the pack being unimportant.
Exclude all PBN / link-scheme / gray-hat mechanisms entirely — the prominence lift must come from legitimate one-time on-page authority and clean links only.
gaps: No source provides a MEASURED magnitude (e.g. 'X more links => Y additional miles of pack reach'). The radius-dilation claim is directional/mechanistic only — flag as such in any reel; do not invent a number.

Could not extract the exact Whitespark 2026 thematic weight TABLE (links % pack vs organic; on-page % pack vs organic) from a primary URL — the report page is JS/gated and the figure circulated by vendor blogs (e.g. 'proximity ~55%') did NOT trace to a primary Whitespark table, so it is intentionally NOT asserted here. Recommend buying/opening the full Whitespark PDF to lock the exact split before reel-binding.

The Joy Hawkins 'links matter more organically than in pack' quote came via search aggregation of Sterling Sky content, not a single confirmed article URL — confirm the exact source article/timestamp before quoting verbatim on camera.
The Moz '88% up from 65%' figure was captured via a vendor (Rio SEO) citing Moz's State of Local SEO; confirm against the primary Moz report for the exact year/wording.

No first-party Google statement was found that explicitly says 'your organic web ranking position' (as opposed to links/reviews) is a pack input — the verbatim Google doc names links + reviews only. The 'web results position' framing lives in the trade-interpretation layer (Search Engine Land), so attribute it there, not to Google.

No source gives a MEASURED magnitude for radius dilation (e.g. 'each authoritative link / X organic rank widens the pack radius by N miles'). The mechanism is well-corroborated directionally; the magnitude remains unquantified — promise direction, not miles.

Could not locate the primary Sterling Sky page hosting the exact 32%/15%/33%/24% table; the figure was verified via a secondary digest (thestacc) that attributes it to the Whitespark 2026 report. Pulling the table from inside the Whitespark report PDF itself would harden it from medium to high confidence.

No roofing/home-services-SPECIFIC dataset showing organic regional dominance widened a contractor's effective lead radius. Roofing sources confirm organic converts well and service-area pages matter, but none isolate the organic->radius effect for the vertical. This stays a general-local-SEO inference applied to roofing.

Pillar is approaching SATURATION on the directional mechanism (organic/authority feeds organic strongly + pack weakly, radius dilates with prominence and is competition-density-dependent). Diminishing returns on further searches for the same thesis; the open frontier is purely a MEASURED magnitude figure, which appears not to exist publicly.

counter.point: The single best independent measurement of what drives the pack (Sterling Sky, 8,186 businesses) found on-page/organic content correlates only SLIGHTLY; the dominant pack levers were review recency and a visible address — NOT website authority.
counter.soWhat: Promise the FLOOR: organic authority supports prominence directionally; do NOT claim a measured radius gain. The pack is won by proximity + review velocity, which is why we never sell the site as the pack-winner.

counter.point: Pack results cluster in a 'tight radius' / 2:1 triangle even in huge metros, and hiding the address can erase the pack entirely — proximity is a hard structural gate that prominence cannot remove.
counter.soWhat: Radius dilation is bounded. Frame it as 'prominence widens the effective radius around a REAL office,' never as ranking anywhere regardless of distance. Distance still caps the pack.

counter.point: Multiple authorities (BrightLocal, Media Captain) model pack and organic as SEPARATE systems with separate factor tables; the 88% 'correlation' figure is marketer BELIEF (Moz survey), not an algorithmic causal measurement.
counter.soWhat: Correlation between organic and local ≠ proof that organic CAUSES pack lift. Keep the claim at 'organic feeds prominence, a stated pack input' (defensible) rather than 'organic ranking lifts pack rank by X' (not measured).

counter.point: Link weight for the pack is small and DROPPING (~8% category, Whitespark/BrightLocal), and Joy Hawkins states link building 'doesn't directly impact local pack rankings.'
counter.soWhat: The link/authority mechanism pays off mostly in ORGANIC (the engine), with only a soft prominence assist to the pack. This is exactly the spine: organic dominance is the prize; the pack is a proximity-capped byproduct.

counter.point: If forced to choose, most local-SEO guidance says PRIORITIZE the local pack over organic for most local businesses — the inverse of King Maker's organic-first framing.
counter.soWhat: Doesn't contradict the mechanism (organic feeds the pack), but it directly contests the OFFER's emphasis. KM's rebuttal must be the high-ticket/regional-scale argument (organic dominance is what scales past a 5-mile pack radius), not a claim that the pack is unimportant. Don't oversell organic-first as universal best practice.

counter.point: Proximity weight quoted as down to ~15% (from 25-30% in 2020) with prominence ~60% comes ONLY from agency blogs that cite no study; the on-point primary pages (SearchEngineLand proximity guide, theoceanmarketing) carry NO such percentages.
counter.soWhat: Do NOT use the 60%/15% prominence-vs-proximity split as a load-bearing claim — it is uncited agency lore. The defensible quantification is the Whitespark on-page 33%-organic-vs-15%-pack asymmetry, not a prominence-beats-proximity percentage.

counter.point: Whitespark's pack-vs-organic weights are an EXPERT-OPINION SURVEY (47 respondents rating factors), not a measured correlation study — a skeptic can dismiss it as crowdsourced perception.
counter.soWhat: Pair the survey weighting with the Sterling Sky link-isolation case studies (measured, named authority) so the asymmetry rests on measured evidence, not opinion alone. Label the Whitespark figure 'modeled/surveyed.'

counter.point: Proximity remains the dominant gate for 'near me' queries (results change within a few streets; tight <3mi urban radius), and the dental-clinic example showing a farther business ranking #1 still sat at only 2.4 km — i.e. prominence stretched the radius modestly, it did not erase distance.
counter.soWhat: Mandatory counterweight: promise the FLOOR (organic dominance + modest pack-radius dilation in less-dense areas), project the CEILING. Never imply the site lets you win the pack across the whole metro from one office.

If your business specializes in some goods, services, or amenities that are hard to find, you may find yourself ranking across a wider radius. ... Prominence relates to how well-known your business is. This is based on signals like the authority of links your website receives.

allClaims.claim: Marketer consensus that organic and local rankings are correlated has risen sharply — a directional signal that organic strength and local visibility move together (does NOT prove causation organic->pack).
allClaims.stat: 88% of marketers agree organic and local search rankings are closely correlated, up from 65% in 2019 (Moz State of Local SEO).
allClaims.snippet: 88% of marketers agree that there is a close correlation between organic and local search rankings. That's up from 65% in 2019.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: measured (survey of marketer belief — belief, not algorithmic measurement; correlation not causation)

allClaims.claim: Independent large-scale study: a deep on-page/organic-content signal correlates only SLIGHTLY with pack ranking — the honest ceiling on 'organic feeds the pack.' On-page content helps, but it is a weak pack lever versus proximity/reviews.

The number of reviews you've gotten this month matters more than your total number of reviews. ... a negative correlation between hiding your address and ranking well in the local pack.

allClaims.snippet: Results are consistently within several miles of each other, with two results close together and one a slightly larger distance away. ... While the distance between points is a bit larger in larger cities, Google consistently shows results in a tight radius.

allClaims.claim: Address/proximity gating is causal, not just correlational: hiding the address (removing the proximity anchor) tanked pack rankings and in one case made the local pack disappear entirely for a keyword — distance is a hard structural input the site cannot override.
allClaims.stat: Real home-service client A/B over time: address hidden -> rankings tanked / pack vanished; address restored -> rankings recovered.
allClaims.snippet: When they hid the address ... the rankings tanked, but when they added the address back a month later, their rankings jumped back up. ... hiding the address caused the local pack to disappear for a main keyword.

allClaims.claim: Prominence-overcomes-proximity is the practitioner-accepted mechanism: a more prominent business slightly farther away can outrank a closer one with weak signals. Confirms direction (authority widens reach) without a measured magnitude.
allClaims.stat: Illustrative: a business ~20 min away with more citations/relevant reviews can outrank one ~3 min away that lacks those signals.
allClaims.snippet: a business that is slightly farther away but significantly more prominent and relevant can still outrank a closer competitor.

allClaims.claim: Google publicly states SEO best practices for the website carry into local — the site's organic strength is a recognized lever on prominence, supporting (not winning) the pack.

allClaims.snippet: Prominence is improved by factors that Google has deemed important such as the presence of plentiful good reviews, website strength, website content (so SEO best practices also apply to local search optimization).

allClaims.snippet: The Local SEO and Organic SEO results are treated as two separate entities. ... You could own two different placements on the first page of Google, one for organic and the other for local.

This is the cleanest corroborator that web/link authority feeds organic far more than the pack.

This is the strongest NEW quantification of 'the site wins organic, only supports the pack.'
