allClaims.measured_or_modeled: directional (Google's stated framework + practitioner observation; not a quantified coefficient)

allClaims.claim: A roofing-vertical local SEO campaign combining review acquisition, service/location pages, and on-page work produced a measured +210% organic sessions and a ramp to 4-5 inbound estimate calls/day plus 38 new Google reviews — all within a 90-day window. This is a directional vendor case study, not an independently audited result, but it gives a concrete roofing-specific shape to the two-conditions thesis: reviews + on-site build moving organic and lead volume together.
allClaims.stat: +210% organic sessions, 38 reviews, 4-5 calls/day in 90 days
allClaims.snippet: +210% total sessions over 90 days; 38 new Google reviews in 90 days; 4-5 inbound estimate calls per day by month 3 (Month 1: 84 calls, Month 2: 112, Month 3: 136); Storm damage/hail repair pages +310%; Service area pages +340%.

allClaims.claim: Reviews have a CAUSAL, quantified effect on revenue — not just on ranking. Harvard Business School's Michael Luca, using a regression-discontinuity design on Washington/Seattle restaurant revenue data, found a one-star increase in Yelp rating causes a 5-9% increase in revenue, and the effect is concentrated in INDEPENDENT (non-chain) businesses — exactly the profile of an owner-operated roofing contractor. This is the strongest independent, peer-grade causal anchor for why a universal review mandate is a genuine business requirement, not a soft nicety.
allClaims.stat: one-star rating increase -> 5-9% revenue increase (causal)
allClaims.snippet: "a one-star increase in Yelp rating leads to a 5-9 percent increase in revenue" and "this effect is driven by independent restaurants; ratings do not affect restaurants with chain affiliation." — Michael Luca, "Reviews, Reputation and Revenue: The Case of Yelp.com," HBS Working Paper No. 12-016 (2011).

allClaims.claim: The FTC has now MOVED from rule to enforcement: on December 22, 2025 it issued its first public enforcement action under the Consumer Review Rule — warning letters to 10 companies — and the current civil penalty is up to $53,088 per violation (an inflation-adjusted increase over the $51,744 figure cited in round 1). The rule explicitly bans review gating, suppressing negative reviews, incentivizing reviews of a specific sentiment, and 'company-controlled review websites.' This makes the 'universal, unscreened ask' the ONLY compliant velocity machine — and the enforcement is now live, not theoretical.
allClaims.stat: First enforcement Dec 22 2025; up to $53,088/violation
allClaims.source_type: primary-independent (Covington law-firm analysis of FTC action; FTC.gov blocks automated fetch)
allClaims.snippet: "The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) sent letters to 10 companies...on December 22, 2025" — "the FTC's first public enforcement action under the Rule." Prohibited: "conditioning incentives on reviews that express a specific sentiment, suppressing negative reviews, the use of so-called 'company-controlled review websites.'" "Violations can result in civil penalties of up to $53,088 per violation."

allClaims.claim: The pack's traffic premium is real but BOUNDED — and the bound validates centering the offer on organic, not the pack. SOCi's study finds top-3 local-pack businesses get 126% more traffic and 93% more actions than ranks 4-10, but only ~42% of local searchers click inside the pack at all. So the pack is a meaningful proximity-capped slice; the majority of local-search engagement (organic + everything else) sits outside it. Promise the pack as a byproduct; sell the organic dominance that captures the larger remainder.
allClaims.stat: +126% traffic / +93% actions for top-3; ~42% click the pack
allClaims.snippet: "Businesses in the Google 3-pack or local pack receive 126% more traffic and 93% more actions (calls, website clicks, and driving directions) than businesses ranked 4-10" and "42% of searchers click on a result inside the local pack or Google 3-pack."
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: measured (vendor-aggregated; corroborates round-1 BrightLocal click split)

allClaims.claim: Review RECENCY hardened sharply in 2025->2026 consumer behavior, reinforcing velocity (not total count) as the live requirement: 74% of consumers seek reviews from the last three months, 32% from the last two weeks (up from 20% the prior year), and 18% are only swayed by reviews from the last week. 97% read reviews, and 68% will only use a business with 4+ stars (up from 55% in 2025). This is the demand-side mirror of Sterling Sky's ~18-day ranking cliff: both the algorithm AND the buyer punish a stale review profile, so a perpetual ask is a dual requirement.
allClaims.stat: 74% want reviews <3mo; 32% <2wk; 18% <1wk; 68% require 4+ stars
allClaims.snippet: "74% seek reviews written in the last three months"; "32% look for reviews written in the last two weeks, a huge jump from last year (20%)"; "18% of consumers are only swayed by reviews written within the last week"; "68% will only use a business with four or more stars, up from 55% in 2025"; "97% of consumers read reviews for local businesses."
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: measured (consumer survey, directional on causation but measured on stated behavior)

pillars.title: Core data-aggregator push
pillars.section:
## L1 — The Data-Aggregator Foundation

**Bottom line.** The aggregator push is a one-time foundation, not a growth lever. We push the client's NAP into the live upstream data pipes — Foursquare, Data Axle, TransUnion/Localeze — so the entity reads clean and consistent across the non-Google ecosystem (Bing, Apple, in-car nav, AI search). It removes a *negative* (inconsistency, stale records, trust loss) and feeds a rising *AI-visibility* signal. It does not, by itself, win the organic rankings — content depth, on-page, and earned links do that. We promise the floor: a clean, owned, durable record. We project the ceiling: AI-search visibility lift. We never promise a ranking jump from citations alone.

**The pipes are alive in 2026 — this is not a dead tactic.** Apple Maps still sources business-listing data from Foursquare, Tripadvisor, and Booking.com, all attributed © 2026 ([apple.com](https://gspe21-ssl.ls.apple.com/html/attribution.html)). Apple's attribution page draws on 50+ listing sources, which is why fixing one upstream record propagates down a long tail ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/local-search-ecosystem/)). The working US set is three: Data Axle (ex-Infogroup), TransUnion Digital Business Profile (ex-Neustar/Localeze), and Foursquare (ex-Factual) — Acxiom exited local in 2019, so the historic "big 4" is now a working three ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/data-aggregators/)). Localeze alone claims 80+ downstream platforms incl. Bing, Apple, Nextdoor — directional, vendor-self-reported ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/data-aggregators/)).

**Citations are a mid-tier classic signal AND a rising AI signal — the defensible framing.** In Whitespark/BrightLocal's 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors survey, citations weigh ~6% of Local Pack and ~7% of Local Organic, but jump to ~13% for AI Search Visibility (tied 2nd) ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/google-local-algorithm-and-ranking-factors/)). The floor-to-ceiling read: a steady classic signal (~6-7%) climbing to a meaningful AI-visibility signal (~13%). Whitespark's 2026 commentary: "with the explosion of AI… citations only seem to be becoming more important" ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/google-local-algorithm-and-ranking-factors/)). Industry-relevant and curated "best-of" placements rank near the top of all 2026 factors — placement quality beats generic volume ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/blog/7-local-search-ranking-factors-that-may-challenge-your-current-thinking/)).

**One-time vs. ongoing.** Owned direct submissions are one-time labor — Whitespark's listings service is explicitly "No subscriptions or contracts" and hands over the username/password for each listing so the business owns it permanently ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/listings-service/)). The structural opposite is Yext's rental: in a documented cancellation case study (n=60, single business), ~60% of listings disappeared or went wrong after the subscription stopped (25% vanished, 35% reverted to incorrect) ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/blog/what-happens-when-you-cancel-yext/)). That is the own-it argument — directional, vendor-incentive, cite as a case study not a controlled study.

**Equity vs. citation — what this lever is NOT.** These are citation/NAP signals — entity-consistency and trust, not link equity. Aggregator records and structured citations are not dofollow backlinks and carry no PageRank-style authority. Do not conflate this lever with the link-equity lever. No PBNs, no link schemes, no gray-hat — excluded by design.

**Approximate one-time cost.** Direct/owned build runs ~$99-$999 per location depending on depth (Data Aggregator tier ~$99) ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/listings-service/)). One caveat to the word "one-time": the TransUnion/Localeze node is itself a small paid annual record (~$99/yr) — the only recurring node in an otherwise own-it build. Frame as "one-time labor with a single small aggregator caveat," not "100% one-time forever" ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/listings-service/)).

**Impact vs. effort.** Low effort, low-but-real impact. High value as a *floor* (clean entity, Bing+Apple coverage, AI-visibility feed); low value as a *ceiling* (will not move the Google pack on its own — ~6% weight). Diminishing returns past the core set. Do it once, do it right, then redirect the dominance narrative to on-page depth and earned links.

**What NOT to oversell:** Do NOT cite "40% more likely to appear in the local pack" — it traces to no primary source and is FTC-exposed false confidence. Do NOT promise a ranking jump from citations alone (~6% pack weight). Do NOT call aggregators a direct Google lever (Google's aggregator use is "likely/unconfirmed" per Whitespark). Do NOT lean on the exact 60/25/35 Yext splits as universal. Treat vendor distribution stats (80+ partners, 500M devices) as directional, never as outcome promises.

loadBearing.claim: Apple Maps still sources business-listing data from Foursquare, Tripadvisor, and Booking.com as of 2026, confirming aggregator/place-data ingestion is alive and feeds the largest non-Google map ecosystem; fixing the upstream record (Foursquare) propagates into Apple Maps.
loadBearing.stat: Apple Maps attribution: 'Business listings data © 2026 Foursquare / © 2026 Tripadvisor / © 2026 Booking.com'; 50+ listing sources
loadBearing.snippet: Business listings data © 2026 Foursquare … Business listings data © 2026 Tripadvisor … Business listings data © 2026 Booking.com
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Primary, first-party Apple proof that the aggregator pipes are LIVE in 2026 — the single strongest rebuttal to 'citations are dead.' Anchors the whole 'why we fix the upstream record' narrative. Re-verified live this session.

loadBearing.claim: Citations are a mid-tier classic local signal (~6-7%) that rises to a meaningful AI-visibility signal (~13%) in the 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors survey — the defensible floor-to-ceiling framing.
loadBearing.stat: Citations: 6% Local Pack, 7% Local Organic, 13% AI Visibility (tied 2nd) — Whitespark/BrightLocal 2026 LSRF
loadBearing.snippet: =Citations (6%) for Local Pack; =Citations (7%) for Local Organic; AI Search Visibility =Citations (13%) tied for second.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The named, survey-sourced replacement for the unverifiable '40%' stat. It quantifies the lever HONESTLY — proves citations matter AND caps the claim at a mid-tier weight, killing over-promise. Re-verified live this session.

loadBearing.claim: Owned citation builds are one-time (no subscription, ownership transferred), whereas Yext is a rental whose listings degrade on cancellation — the structural own-it argument.
loadBearing.stat: Whitespark listings: 'No subscriptions or contracts', ~$99-$999/location one-time; Yext cancellation case study (n=60): ~60% disappeared or went incorrect after cancel
loadBearing.snippet: 'No subscriptions or contracts' … 'Own your listings. Stop renting them' … a username and password for each one. Data Aggregator service $99/location.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This IS the King Maker own-it positioning vs. recurring rental — the offer's spine. Must be framed as one-time labor + single Localeze annual caveat, and the Yext figure cited as a case study (vendor-incentive, n=60) not a controlled study.

loadBearing.claim: The widely-circulated 'consistent NAP = 40% more likely to appear in the local pack' stat does NOT trace to any primary BrightLocal page and must be excluded from reels/pitches.
loadBearing.stat: '40% more likely to appear in local pack' — UNVERIFIED, no primary source
loadBearing.snippet: BrightLocal's primary NAP pages contain no '40%' local-pack stat; it surfaces only on third-party blogs attributing it to 'a BrightLocal study' with no methodology link.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: FTC-exposure landmine. Must be flagged DO-NOT-USE so it never reaches a slide; the verifiable 6/7/13% weights replace it. Excluding it is what makes the pillar defensible.

loadBearing.claim: The working US aggregator set in 2026 is three — Data Axle, TransUnion/Localeze, Foursquare — feeding Bing/Apple/nav/AI; Google's aggregator use is unconfirmed, so this is a foundation/trust+Bing/Apple lever, not a direct Google-pack lever.
loadBearing.stat: 3 primary aggregators (Data Axle, TransUnion Digital Business Profile, Foursquare); Google relationships marked 'likely/unconfirmed'
loadBearing.snippet: Whitespark maps the primary aggregators as Infogroup, Neustar/Localeze, Factual/Foursquare; Google's aggregator relationships are marked likely/unconfirmed.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Defines the scope of the lever and prevents the cardinal over-claim (selling it as a Google-pack growth driver). Keeps the dominance spine pointed at on-page + links.

whatNotToOversell: Do NOT cite '40% more likely to appear in the local pack' — it traces to no primary BrightLocal source and is FTC-exposed false confidence; use the named 6/7/13% LSRF weights instead.
Do NOT promise a ranking jump from citations alone — they are ~6% of Local Pack weight, a mid-tier signal behind reviews, GBP, on-page, and links.
Do NOT call aggregators a direct Google ranking lever — Google's aggregator use is 'likely/unconfirmed'; this is a foundation/trust + Bing/Apple/AI-visibility lever.
Do NOT lean on the exact Yext 60%/25%/35% splits as universal — it is a single-business case study (n=60), vendor-incentive; cite the directional 'lease reverts on cancel' conclusion as a case study.
Do NOT say the build is '100% one-time forever' — the TransUnion/Localeze node is a ~$99/yr paid record; frame as one-time labor with one small recurring aggregator caveat.
Do NOT present vendor distribution stats (80+ partners, 500M devices, 85% of libraries) as outcome promises — they establish the pipes exist, not the magnitude of ranking benefit; label directional.
Do NOT conflate citation/NAP signals with link equity — they are not dofollow backlinks and carry no PageRank-style authority.
Do NOT include any PBN, link-scheme, or gray-hat tactic — explicitly excluded.
gaps: No primary/independent (non-vendor) confirmation that Google currently ingests any specific aggregator feed in 2026 — Whitespark marks all Google relationships 'likely/unconfirmed'; treat Google-via-aggregator as unproven.

The '40% more likely in local pack' NAP stat could not be traced to a primary BrightLocal source; an independent controlled study quantifying citation-consistency -> pack-appearance lift was not found (the 23%/17% figures from secondary 2024/2025 blogs were also untraceable to primary sources).

Exact current free-vs-paid status of a direct Data Axle Express Update submission (whether a basic claim/update is still $0 in 2026) is inferred from the live portal, not from a Data Axle pricing page; worth a direct confirmation before a hard 'free' claim.

No 2026 first-party Foursquare/Apple statement quantifying how reliably a corrected Foursquare record actually propagates into Apple Maps or how long it takes (sync latency is acknowledged as non-instant but unquantified).

Impact-vs-effort is assembled from qualitative signals (low pack weight ~6%, one-time cost, table-stakes) rather than a single sourced effort/ROI study — the read is defensible but modeled, not measured.

No PRIMARY, methodology-linked source anywhere for a quantified NAP-consistency ranking lift (the '40% more likely' figure is unverifiable industry folklore) — the honest ceiling is a directional trust signal, not a number.

No roofing/NC-Triangle-specific MEASURED study isolating citation/aggregator impact on rank; roofing case studies (188% traffic, 145% GBP leads) bundle citations with on-page + GBP + reviews and cannot attribute lift to citations alone.
No published authority/DR figure for the manufacturer-locator backlinks (GAF/CertainTeed/Owens Corning) — their SEO value is asserted/directional, not measured.

Could not load Whitespark's 2026 report page directly (JS-rendered, 402 on Firecrawl); the 2026 figures are sourced via BrightLocal's synthesis of the same survey + Whitespark's own blog — primary survey PDF not captured verbatim.

The exact present-day annual fee for the TransUnion/Localeze aggregator node (round 1 cited ~$99/yr) was not re-verified this pass against a TransUnion-primary page; BrightLocal lists aggregator submissions at ~$60/yr, suggesting the single-recurring-node cost is in the $60-100/yr range — narrow before reel use.

counter.point: Aggregator influence on Google specifically is weaker and less direct than on Bing/Apple. Google increasingly relies on its own crawl, GBP first-party data, and entity understanding rather than buying bulk aggregator feeds; Whitespark only marks Google's aggregator relationships as 'likely/unconfirmed.' So citations are most load-bearing for the broader web/Bing/Apple ecosystem and as a corroborating trust signal — not a direct Google-pack ranking lever.
counter.soWhat: Sell citations as foundation/trust/consistency (and Bing+Apple coverage), NOT as a pack-ranking growth lever. This is consistent with the LSRF showing citations at only ~6% of pack weight.

counter.point: Most aggregator distribution stats (80+ partners, 500M devices, 85% of libraries) are vendor self-reported marketing claims, not independently audited. They establish that the pipes exist, not the magnitude of ranking benefit.
counter.soWhat: Use them to justify 'why we fix the upstream record' — never to promise a ranking outcome. Label directional.

counter.point: Citations are explicitly table-stakes with diminishing returns: once NAP is consistent across the core set, adding more citations yields little. They will not, on their own, win organic regional dominance (the spine) — links and on-page do the organic heavy lifting.
counter.soWhat: Position the aggregator push as a one-time foundation that removes a NEGATIVE (inconsistency/penalty risk), then redirect the dominance narrative to on-page + earned links.

counter.point: The Yext-cancellation study (n=60, single business) is a Whitespark blog with a direct commercial interest in selling its Yext-replacement service — vendor-incentive and a tiny sample.
counter.soWhat: The directional conclusion (lease reverts on cancel) is corroborated by Yext's own model and multiple independent forums, so it holds — but cite it as 'a documented case study' not 'a controlled study,' and avoid leaning on the exact 60%/25%/35% splits as universal.

counter.point: The widely-circulated 'businesses with consistent NAP are 40% more likely to appear in the local pack' stat STILL does not trace to a primary BrightLocal page. Round 1 flagged it; round 2 confirms it is now even repeated on BrightLocal's own /learn synthesis page AND across secondary blogs (Prose, ServiceTitan-adjacent) but always as 'a BrightLocal study' with NO methodology link or primary citation. It behaves like an industry-laundered figure.
counter.soWhat: DO NOT put '40% more likely' in a reel or pitch — it is FTC-exposed false-confidence. Cite the verifiable Whitespark/BrightLocal 2026 weights (6%/7%/13%) instead, which are sourced to a named survey. Treat NAP consistency as a TRUST/table-stakes signal, not a quantified ranking lever.

counter.point: Citations are only ~6-7% of classic local ranking weight — a mid-tier signal, well behind reviews, GBP signals, and on-page/links. A skeptic can correctly say 'citation building alone will not move rankings.' Joy Hawkins (Sterling Sky) explicitly de-emphasizes bulk citation building as evolved/low-value busywork.
counter.soWhat: Position the aggregator/citation push as FOUNDATION (trust + AI-visibility + NAP integrity), NOT as the growth engine. The organic-dominance engine is content depth + on-page + reviews; citations keep the entity clean and feed AI. Promise the floor (consistency/ownership/AI-visibility), never a ranking-jump from citations alone.

counter.point: The strongest pro-thesis quantitative claims (the $2/site, $60/yr, 'data removed on non-payment', and 30-day reversion) come from vendors who SELL the manual alternative — BrightLocal and K2Z Digital. Vendor-incentive bias is present.
counter.soWhat: The vendor pricing is independently corroborated by the round-1 Whitespark cancellation study (measured: ~60% of Yext listings disappeared/went wrong after cancellation), so the OWN-IT thesis survives. But cite the measured Whitespark study as the load-bearing proof and use vendor pricing only as a cost illustration, flagged as vendor-sourced.

counter.point: The 'Google now ingests local data directly so aggregators are dying' thesis — the skeptic's strongest attack on this pillar — has NO primary support. Searches for Google deprecating third-party local-data sources returned only cookie/structured-data-deprecation news, nothing about local-listing aggregators losing relevance.
counter.soWhat: This is actually FAVORABLE: the 'aggregators are dead' narrative is unsubstantiated. Combined with Apple Maps' confirmed 50+/aggregator ingestion (round 1) and Whitespark 2026 showing citations RISING for AI, the upstream-record thesis is defensible. Do not concede 'aggregators are obsolete' in a pitch — there is no primary evidence for it.

allClaims.claim: Apple Maps explicitly sources business-listing/POI data from Foursquare, Tripadvisor, and Booking.com as of 2026 — confirming aggregator/place-data ingestion is alive and feeds the largest non-Google map ecosystem. Maintaining the upstream place record (Foursquare) propagates into Apple Maps.

allClaims.snippet: Business listings data © 2026 Foursquare … Business listings data © 2026 Tripadvisor … Business listings data © 2026 Booking.com (TomTom listed only for traffic incident data, not business listings).

allClaims.claim: Foursquare remains a primary location-data provider in 2026 (post-Factual merger), not a defunct directory — it carries one of the world's largest place datasets and feeds downstream apps and Apple Maps. It is a live upstream record worth keeping accurate.
allClaims.stat: Foursquare Places spans 500M+ devices / one of the largest location datasets in the world
allClaims.snippet: Foursquare now has one of the largest location data sets in the world, spanning more than 500 million devices.

allClaims.claim: The current US aggregator triad that still feeds the local ecosystem is Data Axle (formerly Infogroup), TransUnion Digital Business Profile (formerly Neustar/Localeze), and Foursquare (formerly Factual). This is the present-day 'big set' — Acxiom exited directory/local in 2019, so the historic 'big 4' is now effectively a working three.
allClaims.stat: 3 primary aggregators: Data Axle, TransUnion Digital Business Profile (ex-Neustar/Localeze), Foursquare
allClaims.snippet: BrightLocal names three main local data aggregators: Foursquare (Foursquare Places), Data Axle (formerly Infogroup), and TransUnion Digital Business Profile (formerly Neustar Localeze).

allClaims.claim: Independent corroboration of the aggregator set: Whitespark's ecosystem map identifies the primary US aggregators historically as Infogroup, Neustar/Localeze, Factual, and Foursquare, and Apple Maps alone draws on '50+ sources of business listings data' — i.e. aggregators feed a long downstream tail, which is why fixing data upstream propagates broadly.
allClaims.stat: Apple Maps attributions page features 50+ sources of business listings data
allClaims.snippet: Apple Maps attributions page features more than 50 sources of business listings data; Whitespark maps the primary aggregators as Infogroup, Neustar/Localeze, Factual, and Foursquare (Foursquare replacing Acxiom after its 2019 directory closure).

allClaims.claim: CORRECTION to the seed: 'Express Update defunct 2021' is FALSE. Data Axle's Express Update / Local Listings remains an active, free claim-and-update channel in 2026 — the login/claim portal is live and businesses can create or claim a profile at no cost. Do NOT claim Express Update is dead; the correct framing is that direct free submission to Data Axle still exists (Acxiom is the aggregator that exited local, in 2019).
allClaims.stat: Express Update / Data Axle Local Listings login portal: live, free claim
allClaims.snippet: Active Express Update / Data Axle local-listings login interface: 'Head to Express Update to find and claim your business' — claim is free, no fee shown.

allClaims.claim: Yext is LEASE-not-own, proven by a measured cancellation study: of 60 listings Yext reported as synced, after cancellation only ~40% stayed correct (3 manually-claimed-correct + 21 correct-but-unsynced = 35%+5%), 35% reverted to incorrect, and 25% disappeared entirely — i.e. ~60% disappeared or went wrong. This is the defensible basis for King Maker's own-it positioning: stop paying and the listings degrade.
allClaims.stat: 60 listings tested: 25% disappeared, 35% reverted to incorrect, ~40% stayed correct; '60% disappeared or featured incorrect information' after cancellation
allClaims.snippet: 60 listings Yext reported as synced … 15 listings disappeared (25%), 21 became incorrect (35%), 21 remained correct but unsynced (35%), 3 remained synced/claimed (5%); '60% of the listings disappeared or started featuring incorrect information after the subscription was canceled.'

allClaims.claim: Owned/direct citation builds are a ONE-TIME cost, not a subscription. Whitespark's listings service is explicitly one-time-fee, no subscription/contract, and hands over usernames and passwords so the business owns each listing permanently — the structural opposite of Yext's recurring rental.
allClaims.stat: One-time fee; packages ~$99-$999/location (Data Aggregator tier $99); 'No subscriptions or contracts'
allClaims.snippet: 'No subscriptions or contracts' … 'Own your listings. Stop "renting" them from other services' … 'a username and password for each one — just as if you created them yourself!' Data Aggregator service $99/location; packages to $999/location, one-time fee.

allClaims.claim: One nuance on 'one-time': the TransUnion/Localeze aggregator record is itself a paid annual subscription (~$99/yr) — the only paid node inside an otherwise own-it citation build. After year one the listing persists but you can't push edits unless you re-claim. Frame the build as one-time labor with a single recurring aggregator caveat, not '100% one-time forever.'
allClaims.stat: TransUnion Digital Business Profile ~$99/year; Localeze account requires payment when newly created
allClaims.snippet: 'The only site included in our service that requires payment is Localeze, when a new account is created.' (BrightLocal separately lists TransUnion Digital Business Profile at '$99 per year for a business profile.')

allClaims.claim: TransUnion Digital Business Profile (ex-Localeze) is the aggregator with the widest declared distribution and is the de facto Bing/Apple feeder — it claims partnerships with 80+ search platforms, apps, and navigation systems (incl. Bing, Apple, Nextdoor). This is why the Localeze node is the one citation worth its small annual fee.
allClaims.stat: TransUnion Digital Business Profile: 80+ partner platforms/apps/navigation systems
allClaims.snippet: TransUnion Digital Business Profile boasts partnerships with over 80 search platforms, mobile applications, navigation systems, directories, and more — examples include NextDoor, Bing, and Apple.

allClaims.claim: Data Axle's declared distribution backs its place in the set: it claims feeds to leading in-car navigation systems, 85% of large public libraries, and the leading search engines — i.e. correcting the Data Axle record propagates to navigation/search downstream.
allClaims.stat: Data Axle: partnerships with leading in-car nav, 85% of large public libraries, leading search engines
allClaims.snippet: Data Axle claims partnerships 'with the leading in-car navigation systems, 85% of large public libraries, and the leading search engines.'

allClaims.claim: NAP/citation consistency is a defensible signal on TRUST and consumer behavior — the safe stat to cite. BrightLocal's primary content states a large majority lose trust over inconsistent contact details, and citations are a confirmed top-5 local-pack ranking factor in the LSRF. This is the honest framing: consistency is table-stakes foundation, not a growth lever.
allClaims.stat: 80% say they will lose trust due to inconsistent contact details; 93% of consumers frustrated by incorrect info; citations a top-5 local ranking factor
allClaims.snippet: '80% say they will lose trust due to inconsistent contact details' … 'Many citations with identical NAP information can signal to Google that what it knows about a business is correct' … citations cited as a top-five ranking factor via the Local SEO Ranking Factors Survey.

allClaims.claim: DO-NOT-USE FLAG: the widely-circulated 'businesses with consistent NAP are 40% more likely to appear in the local pack' stat attributed to BrightLocal does NOT trace to any primary BrightLocal page (checked /what-is-nap and /nap-data-accuracy — neither contains it); it only appears on secondary SEO blogs citing 'a BrightLocal study' with no link. Treat it as unverified, exactly like the unverifiable '55% proximity' figure — do not put it in a reel/pitch.
allClaims.stat: '40% more likely to appear in local pack' — UNVERIFIED, no primary source found
allClaims.snippet: BrightLocal's own primary NAP pages contain no '40%' local-pack stat; the figure surfaces only on third-party blogs (e.g. yadavbikash.com) attributing it to 'a BrightLocal study' without a traceable citation.

allClaims.claim: Citations are NOT obsolete — they rose in relevance in 2026 because AI search engines lean on them. In Whitespark's 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors (the industry's largest survey), citation signals weigh ~6% of Local Pack and ~7% of Local Organic rankings, but jump to ~13% for AI search visibility (tied for second among AI-visibility factors). This is the defensible FLOOR-to-CEILING framing: citations are a steady mid-tier classic-ranking signal AND a rising AI-visibility signal — not a dying tactic.
allClaims.stat: Citations: 6% Local Pack, 7% Local Organic, 13% AI visibility (tied 2nd) — Whitespark/BrightLocal 2026 LSRF
allClaims.snippet: '=Citations (6%)' for Local Pack rankings and '=Citations (7%)' for Local Organic rankings (2026 survey). AI Search Visibility: '=Citations (13%)' tied for second place. 'After a period of questioning whether citations still matter to local SEO, with the explosion of AI over the last few years citations only seem to be becoming more important in business visibility.'

allClaims.claim: Whitespark's 2026 report ranks specific citation factors near the TOP of all local-search factors: presence on expert-curated 'best of' lists (#1), prominence on key industry-relevant domains (#3), quality/authority of unstructured citations (#4), quantity of unstructured citations (#7), quantity of citations from industry-relevant domains (#15). 'Both structured and unstructured citations are dominating the AI visibility scenario.' This is the strongest 2026 corroboration that the citation foundation matters — and that industry-relevant placement beats generic volume.
allClaims.stat: Citation 'best-of lists' = #1 factor; industry-relevant domains = #3; unstructured citation quality = #4 (Whitespark 2026)
allClaims.snippet: 'AI is bringing citations of all kinds back into the digital marketing limelight.' Factors: 'Presence of business on expert-curated best of and similar lists' (#1); 'Prominence on key industry-relevant domains' (#3); 'Quality/authority of unstructured citations' (#4). 'Both structured and unstructured citations are dominating the AI visibility scenario.'

allClaims.claim: Hard one-time-vs-rental cost proof, primary source: BrightLocal's own pricing is manual citation submissions from ~$2/site and data-aggregator submissions ~$60/year, versus Yext at $200-$500/year — and with the one-off build the listings stay yours, whereas 'if you don't pay the [Yext] charges, your business information is removed from the sites in their network.' This is the defensible economic spine of King Maker's own-it positioning: a one-time build is a fraction of a recurring rental AND it persists when you stop paying.
allClaims.stat: BrightLocal: $2/site manual, ~$60/yr aggregators vs Yext $200-$500/yr; Yext data removed on non-payment
allClaims.snippet: 'Manual Citation Submissions from just $2/site' and 'Data Aggregator Submissions costing just $60/year,' while Yext charges 'between $200-$500 dollars per year.' Regarding Yext: 'if you don't pay the charges, your business information is removed from the sites in their network.'

allClaims.claim: The recommended professional approach is the HYBRID King Maker already implies: manually claim/submit the most important 25-50 sites for control + quick results, then use the data aggregators for wide downstream distribution. BrightLocal (the vendor that sells both) does not recommend bulk automated-only; it recommends a one-time manual core plus aggregator distribution — corroborating that a one-time labor build (not a subscription) is the right shape.
allClaims.stat: Hybrid: claim top 25-50 sites manually + aggregators for wide distribution
allClaims.snippet: The article advises a hybrid strategy: 'submit and claim your listing on the most important 25-50 sites' manually for quick results, then use aggregators 'to get wide distribution to hundreds of sites/services.'

allClaims.claim: ROOFING-VERTICAL refinement (Joy Hawkins / Sterling Sky, the most-cited independent local-SEO authority): do NOT build hundreds of generic citations — target industry-specific directories. For roofing that means the high-authority manufacturer locators and trade directories (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster contractor-finders; HomeAdvisor/Angi/Houzz/Thumbtack/BBB) over volume. This is the defensible ROI read: a tight set of relevant, ownable citations beats bulk submission, which Joy treats as low-value busywork.
allClaims.stat: Quality industry-specific directories > hundreds of generic citations (Joy Hawkins)
allClaims.snippet: 'Citations used to be the backbone of local SEO, but their role has evolved. For Joy, it's all about industry-specific directories. Rather than advocating for building hundreds of citations, Joy's approach focuses on quality over quantity by targeting industry-specific directories that are most relevant to a business.'

allClaims.claim: Roofing manufacturer contractor-locators are a real, ownable, vertical-specific citation node — primary pages confirm GAF, CertainTeed, and Owens Corning each operate a public ZIP-code contractor finder listing the contractor's name, address, and phone (NAP) and gated by current certification. Earning the certification (one-time qualification) yields a durable high-authority citation a generic competitor cannot buy. Label: directional on SEO weight (no published DR/ranking-lift figure), but verified as an existing ownable placement.
allClaims.stat: GAF/CertainTeed/Owens Corning each run a public NAP-bearing certified-contractor locator
allClaims.snippet: GAF offers a Find a Contractor tool; the official contractor locator allows homeowners to enter their ZIP code and view certified contractors 'with business addresses, phone numbers, and specialization areas, filtering results to show only those contractors who maintain current certification.'
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: directional (existence verified; SEO weight not quantified)

pillars.title: Tier-1 manual citations
pillars.section:
## L2 — The Tier-1 Citation Foundation

**Bottom line:** Citations are a one-time foundation, not a growth lever. We build the tier-1 set once, verify NAP is consistent, and stop. They are table-stakes — own them and move the budget to organic links, reviews, and the deep site.

**Direct ranking weight is low and falling.** The 2026 Whitespark Local Search Ranking Factors report (47-expert survey, released Nov 6 2025) puts citation signals at 6% for the Local Pack and 7% for Local Organic — sixth of eight factors ([advicelocal.com](https://www.advicelocal.com/blog/2026-local-search-ranking-factors-maps-organic-ai/)). Moz's series shows the same trajectory: citations fell from 13% (2020) to 7% ([thehoth.com](https://www.thehoth.com/learn/local/seo/ranking-factors/)). The organic engine we center is on-page (33%) + links (24%) — citations are not where rank is won.

**The real modern reason to build them is the AI/answer layer.** In the same Whitespark report, citation signals jump to 13% / third place for AI-search visibility, and three of the top five AI factors are citation-related ([advicelocal.com](https://www.advicelocal.com/blog/2026-local-search-ranking-factors-maps-organic-ai/)). ChatGPT-class engines pull location data from Bing + Foursquare; Apple Maps powers Siri. So the foundation feeds the answer engines — that is the defensible "why," not a backlink or pack-rank claim.

**One-time vs ongoing.** This is a ONE-TIME build (~35 citations) that we own permanently. Experts are explicit that continuing to add citations "at a steady rate doesn't have the same level of impact" as the initial foundation ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/expert-local-citation-survey/)). We do NOT sell ongoing citation management, and we avoid lease-model aggregators (Yext-style) that revert when payment stops. We build direct and permanent.

**DoFollow (link equity) vs NoFollow (citation only).** Most tier-1 directories are NoFollow — they carry NAP/entity/referral value, not link equity: BBB, Foursquare, Houzz, Yellow Pages, Angi, Thumbtack, Trustpilot, Facebook all pass NoFollow ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/top-citation-sites/general/dofollow-nofollow/)). The DoFollow subset worth prioritizing for any equity rationale: Google Business Profile, Apple Business Connect, Bing Places, HomeAdvisor, Nextdoor ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/top-citation-sites/general/dofollow-nofollow/)). Spot-check: do NOT claim Yelp is DoFollow — its links are redirected and carry rel=nofollow; one vendor table mislabels it ([digitalwebsolutions.com](https://www.digitalwebsolutions.com/resources/top-citation-sites/general/dofollow-nofollow/)). DA numbers are a Moz proxy, not a Google ranking factor — present them as rough authority signal only ([thehoth.com](https://www.thehoth.com/learn/local/seo/ranking-factors/)).

**Approximate one-time cost.** Tier A (free, DoFollow, AI-relevant): Google Business Profile, Apple Business Connect, Bing Places, Nextdoor — $0 ([businessconnect.apple.com](https://businessconnect.apple.com/)). Tier B (free/freemium, high-DA, NoFollow): Yelp, Foursquare, Houzz, Yellow Pages — $0. Tier D NC credential anchor: NCLBGC license profile (~76,160 NC contractor records) — free, credential-gated, unreplicable by thin/unlicensed competitors ([portal.nclbgc.org](http://portal.nclbgc.org/Public/Search)). The only recurring costs are Tier C trust listings — Chamber of Commerce (~$125/yr, DoFollow + indexed, bought as much for networking as SEO) and BBB (paid accreditation, NoFollow) ([localsearchforum.com](https://localsearchforum.com/threads/backlinks-like-local-bbb-and-local-area-chambers-of-commerce-worth-paying-for.52423/)) — both sold as trust/badge value, never as backlinks. Net: the high-leverage core is effectively $0 in hard cost.

**Impact vs effort.** Low direct rank impact, low effort, high necessity. Beyond rank, business-directory pages occupy ~31% of the top-10 organic results for the average local search, so a correct citation can itself surface in the SERP and intercept a click ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/business-listings-visibility-study/)). The floor we promise: consistent NAP, AI-citability, possible SERP/referral interception. The ceiling we project: marginal entity-corroboration lift via Google's 2020 "nofollow-as-hint" reclassification — directional, not a ranking promise ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/resources/top-citation-sites/general/dofollow-nofollow/)).

**What NOT to oversell:** citations are not backlinks, not a ranking lever, and not a recurring product. Promise the floor, project the ceiling.

loadBearing.claim: Citation signals carry low and declining direct local-ranking weight: 6% Local Pack / 7% Local Organic per the most recent (2026) Whitespark expert survey, down from a Moz-measured 13% in 2020 to 7%. Citations are table-stakes, not a growth lever.
loadBearing.stat: Citations = 6% Local Pack (6th of 8), 7% Local Organic; Moz trend 13% (2020) to 7%
loadBearing.snippet: Local Pack/Maps: Citations rank 6th at 6%. Local Organic: Citations rank 6th (tied) at 7%. Local Pack top 3: Google Business Profile 32%, Reviews 20%, On-Page 15%.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the anchor that justifies the entire 'build once, then stop' offer framing and protects against an FTC-exposed over-promise that citations move rankings. If wrong, the offer's scoping logic collapses.

loadBearing.claim: The defensible modern value of citations is AI-search visibility, not link equity or pack rank: citation signals rank 3rd at 13% for AI visibility in the same 2026 Whitespark report, with three of the top five AI factors citation-related.
loadBearing.stat: Citations = 13% / 3rd for AI visibility (vs 6% pack, 7% organic); top AI factors On-Page 24%, Reviews 16%, Citations 13%
loadBearing.snippet: AI Search Visibility: Citations rank 3rd at 13%. 'Three of the top five factors for AI are related to citations.'
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the slide/reel headline reframe — it is the single honest reason to build the foundation. If it does not hold, we have no positive case for citations and must reposition to pure NAP-consistency.

loadBearing.claim: Most tier-1 citation directories pass NoFollow links (citation/entity/referral value, not link equity); a DoFollow subset (GBP, Apple, Bing, HomeAdvisor, Nextdoor) is the higher-equity foundational set. Do not sell NoFollow citations as backlinks.
loadBearing.stat: NoFollow: BBB 91, Foursquare 91, Houzz 86, Angi 76, Thumbtack 76, YP 62. DoFollow: GBP 100, Apple 99, Bing 93-94, HomeAdvisor 78, Nextdoor 78-83
loadBearing.snippet: NoFollow table: Facebook 94, Trustpilot 92, BBB 91, Foursquare 91, Houzz 86, Angi 76, Thumbtack 76. DoFollow table: GBP 100, Apple 99, Bing Maps 93, HomeAdvisor 78, Nextdoor 83.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This governs how we describe every citation in the pitch — equity vs citation value. A vendor-incentive source, so it needs spot-verification (the Yelp mislabel proves the tables are not authoritative). Directly FTC-exposed if we call a NoFollow citation a 'backlink.'

loadBearing.claim: Do NOT claim Yelp is DoFollow — Yelp links are redirected and carry rel=nofollow, despite one vendor table listing it DoFollow. Treat Yelp as a high-DA NoFollow citation.
loadBearing.stat: Yelp DA 93; links redirected + nofollow (NOT dofollow as one vendor table claims)
loadBearing.snippet: Yelp 93 NoFollow. 'links from Yelp are redirected, and links from Yelp are guaranteed to have a nofollow tag.'
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: A concrete error-correction that would land in a pitch if uncaught — proves the discipline of spot-verifying vendor tables at build time. Protects credibility on a directory every roofer recognizes.

loadBearing.claim: Business-directory pages occupy ~31% of the top-10 organic results for the average local search, so a correctly-built citation can itself surface in the SERP and intercept the click even when it passes no link equity. This is the defensible 'why bother with NoFollow citations' answer.
loadBearing.stat: ~31% of top-10 organic results for average local search are business-directory pages (~3 of top 10)
loadBearing.snippet: Business directories make up almost a third (31%) of the top ten organic search results overall.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Supplies the SERP-real-estate rationale that lets us promise a floor (possible click interception) without promising a ranking lift. Vendor-incentive source — needs independent corroboration before it anchors a slide.

whatNotToOversell: Never call NoFollow citations (BBB, Yelp, Foursquare, Houzz, Angi, Thumbtack, Facebook, Trustpilot) 'backlinks' or imply link equity — they are citation/entity/referral value only.
Do not claim Yelp is DoFollow — its links are redirected and nofollow; one vendor table mislabels it.
Do not sell citations as a ranking lever — direct pack weight is ~6% and falling. Position as a one-time AI-feed + NAP-trust foundation only.
Do not pitch ongoing/recurring citation management — incremental citations past the foundation are low-ROI and self-undo (drift, lease-model reversion).
Do not present Moz DA numbers as a Google ranking factor — DA is a third-party proxy; Google does not use it.
Do not conflate the free Angi/HomeAdvisor profile (citation value) with their paid pay-per-lead product ($15-$120+/shared lead).
Promise the FLOOR (consistent NAP, AI-citability, possible SERP/referral interception), project the CEILING (marginal nofollow-as-hint corroboration) — never promise a rank gain.
Treat any single dofollow/nofollow/DA figure as needing live spot-verification at build time — vendor tables disagree and are dated.
gaps: No single PRIMARY (non-vendor) source compiles DA + dofollow/nofollow per site — DA is inherently a Moz/Ahrefs proprietary metric, so a fully primary table does not exist; corroboration is cross-vendor + behavioral (Yelp redirect/nofollow) rather than first-party.

Exact one-time cost per manual citation submission not nailed to a primary source this pass (BrightLocal Citation Builder ~$2-3.20/site, Whitespark ~$4-5/site cited via search summary, not fetched on-page).
Did not confirm whether Nextdoor's business-page external link is currently dofollow on the live page (two vendor tables agree DoFollow but it should be spot-verified at build).
NC local Chamber of Commerce specifics (which Charlotte/Raleigh chamber, exact fee, dofollow on the live member page) not individually verified — generalized from the $125/yr expert datapoint.
BBB accreditation exact fee not pinned to a primary BBB page this pass.

No NC/Triangle-SPECIFIC citation ranking data surfaced (NCLBGC + local Chamber from round 1 remain the only NC-specific anchors; roofing-vertical case studies found were vendor-authored and weakly quantified — e.g. rohringresults 'before #7 -> after MAP rank 1.9' but NO citation count, time period, or dollar figures disclosed, so treat as vendor-incentive directional only).

The Whitespark 2026 percentages were captured via a secondary agency summary (advicelocal) because the primary whitespark.ca page is JS-rendered and did not yield the figures to WebFetch — RECOMMEND a verifier re-confirm the 6%/7%/13% splits directly against whitespark.ca/local-search-ranking-factors before any of these land verbatim in a pitch.

The SE Ranking 1% -> 53.5% AI-citation threshold is a single-vendor figure; directionally corroborated by Foundation/AirOps + BrightLocal but not independently replicated — keep labeled medium-confidence.

No measured study isolating the INCREMENTAL ranking/AI-visibility lift of going from a foundational ~35 citations to a larger set for a ROOFING contractor specifically (the diminishing-returns claim is general-vertical).

Firecrawl was out of credits (402) the entire session; all gathering done via WebSearch + WebFetch. A scrape-confirm pass on the live Whitespark and BrightLocal pages was not possible for the JS-rendered Whitespark figures.

counter.point: DA (Domain Authority) is a Moz proprietary third-party metric, NOT a Google ranking factor — citing 'DA 91' as link value can mislead. Google does not use DA; it is a relative proxy. The ranking-relevant question is dofollow status + topical relevance + Google's own prominence calc, not the DA number.
counter.soWhat: Rank the citation set by dofollow + relevance + free/paid, and present DA only as a rough authority proxy with that caveat — never imply DA itself moves rankings.

counter.point: Vendor citation tables disagree on dofollow/nofollow and DA (BrightLocal says Yelp DoFollow; others say NoFollow; Houzz listed 86 vs 90; Yellow Pages 62 vs 87). These are scraped/dated and vendor-incentivized.
counter.soWhat: Treat any single dofollow/nofollow claim as needing spot-verification on the live page at build time; the Yelp flag proves the tables are not authoritative.

counter.point: Citation signals are only ~7% of pack weight and falling, and 0% of the ORGANIC-dominance engine that KM centers — citations are pure table-stakes, not a growth lever. Over-investing in citation volume is the classic low-ROI trap.
counter.soWhat: Position citations as a one-time foundation that must simply be CORRECT/consistent; route the budget and the offer headline to organic links (~24%) + reviews + on-page, per the spine.

counter.point: Self-managed monthly citation 'services' self-undo: many directories let listings drift or get overwritten, and lease-model aggregators (Yext) revert when you stop paying — so a 'volume of citations' deliverable creates a maintenance liability.
counter.soWhat: Deliver permanent/direct manual citations once (own them), not a leased recurring feed; this is honest AND a differentiator vs Yext-style competitors.

counter.point: The skeptic's strongest case is NOT that citations have zero correlation — no such study surfaced — it is that citations are explicitly described by experts as 'nowhere near as powerful or important as they used to be,' an 'old-school Local SEO tactic,' with the direct pack-ranking weight halved over the last cycle (Moz 13%->7%, Whitespark down to 6%). The honest implication: do NOT sell citations as a ranking lever. The defensible value has migrated to AI-visibility + NAP-trust + the directory page itself surfacing in the SERP.
counter.soWhat: Frame the tier-1 build as a one-time AI-feed + entity-trust foundation, never as a pack-rank or backlink lever. Promise the FLOOR (consistent NAP, AI-citability, possible SERP/referral interception), not a ranking gain. This protects against an FTC-exposed over-promise.

counter.point: Continuing to build citations 'at a steady rate doesn't have the same level of impact' as the initial foundation — i.e. ongoing/recurring citation building is low-ROI. This is the skeptic's case against any recurring citation SKU.
counter.soWhat: Reinforces scoping the deliverable as a ONE-TIME ~35-citation foundation (in-scope per the pillar rules) and explicitly NOT selling ongoing citation management. Aligns with the 'one-time shippable off-page is IN scope, ongoing is OUT' rule.

counter.point: AI-citation volume is dominated by directories the business does NOT fully control (Yelp, BBB, Angi) and by the business's OWN website (58% in ChatGPT) — NOT by the breadth of the citation footprint. A skeptic argues the marginal citation beyond the GBP+Yelp+Foursquare+own-site core adds little AI visibility.
counter.soWhat: Confirms the SPINE: the deep authority SITE is the highest-leverage AI-cited asset (own website = single most-cited source); citations are a thin supporting foundation, not the engine. Do not let the citation deliverable inflate into the headline.

counter.point: Angi/HomeAdvisor/Thumbtack DO rank highly in AI-citation volume (round-1 flagged them as lead-gen marketplaces), which could tempt over-claiming. But their citation presence is a free-profile byproduct; the rankings reflect the platforms' own SEO/AI weight, not the contractor's effort — and the paid lead product is a separate, adversarial channel.
counter.soWhat: Claim only the free profile for AI-citation/entity value; never imply the paid lead product is part of the SEO foundation. Honesty rule from round 1 holds and is reinforced by the volume data.

allClaims.claim: The majority of tier-1 citation directories pass NoFollow links — they carry NAP/citation value and AI-feed value, NOT link equity. BBB (DA 91, NoFollow), Foursquare (DA 91, NoFollow), Houzz (DA 86-90, NoFollow), Yellow Pages (DA 62-87, NoFollow), Angi (DA 76, NoFollow), Thumbtack (DA 76, NoFollow), Trustpilot (DA 92, NoFollow), Facebook (DA 94, NoFollow). The honest implication: do not sell these as 'backlinks' — sell them as foundational consistency/entity citations.
allClaims.stat: BBB 91 NoFollow; Foursquare 91 NoFollow; Houzz 86 NoFollow; Angi 76 NoFollow; Thumbtack 76 NoFollow; Yellow Pages 62 NoFollow
allClaims.snippet: NoFollow Links table: Facebook 94, Instagram 93, Trustpilot 92, Waze 92, BBB 91, Foursquare 91, Houzz 86, Angi 76, Thumbtack 76, Yellow Pages CA 62 — all NoFollow.

allClaims.claim: A subset of tier-1 citations DO pass DoFollow links, making them the higher-equity foundational set: Google Business Profile (DA 100, DoFollow), Apple Business Connect (DA ~99, DoFollow), Bing/Bing Maps (DA 93-94, DoFollow), HomeAdvisor (DA 78, DoFollow), Nextdoor (DA 78-83, DoFollow). These are the citations worth prioritizing for any link-equity rationale; the rest are citation-value only.
allClaims.stat: GBP 100, Apple 99, Bing 93-94, HomeAdvisor 78, Nextdoor 78-83 — DoFollow
allClaims.snippet: DoFollow Links table: Google Business Profile 100, Apple Business Connect 99, LinkedIn 99, WebMD 94, Yelp 93, TripAdvisor 93, Bing Maps 93, Zillow 89, Nextdoor 83, HomeAdvisor 78.

allClaims.claim: DISCREPANCY FLAGGED — do NOT claim Yelp is DoFollow. BrightLocal's own table lists Yelp (DA 93) as DoFollow, but Yelp links are redirected and carry the rel=nofollow attribute; multiple independent sources confirm Yelp is NoFollow. Treat Yelp as a high-DA NoFollow citation (referral + trust value, not link equity). This is the kind of vendor-table error that must be corrected before it lands in a pitch.
allClaims.stat: Yelp DA 93; link is redirected + nofollow (NOT dofollow as one vendor table claims)
allClaims.snippet: Yelp 93 NoFollow (DigitalWebSolutions citation table). Independent sources: 'links from Yelp are redirected, and links from Yelp are guaranteed to have a nofollow tag.'

allClaims.claim: Apple Business Connect and Bing Places for Business are both FREE to claim and are the highest-leverage non-Google foundational citations because they feed AI/assistant search — ChatGPT pulls heavily from Bing + Foursquare, Apple Maps powers Siri/iPhone. This is the strongest defensible reason to prioritize them beyond NAP consistency.
allClaims.stat: $0 to claim both; ChatGPT pulls 70%+ of local data from Foursquare and uses Bing heavily
allClaims.snippet: Apple Business Connect: 'free tool' to claim and optimize location place cards. Bing Places: 'free local business directory.' AI-search sources: ChatGPT uses Bing/Foursquare; Apple Maps powers Siri.

allClaims.claim: Citations are TABLE-STAKES with diminishing returns: citation signals carry only ~7% of local-pack ranking weight per Moz's Local Search Ranking Factors, and that weight has DECLINED from 13% (2020) to 7% — confirming the seed thesis that you build the foundation once and stop. Volume past the foundational set is low-ROI.
allClaims.stat: Citation signals ~7% of local-pack ranking weight (down from 13% in 2020); link signals ~13%
allClaims.snippet: Moz Local Search Ranking Factors: GBP 36%, on-page 16%, reviews 15%, links 13%, citations 7%, behavioral 7%, personalization 6%. Citations declined 13% (2020) to 7%.

allClaims.claim: Citations still matter for VISIBILITY beyond ranking weight: business directory pages occupy ~31% of the top-10 organic results for the average local search — meaning a foundational citation can itself surface in the SERP and intercept the click even when it passes no link equity. This is the defensible 'why bother with nofollow citations' answer.
allClaims.stat: ~31% of top-10 organic results for average local search are business directory pages (~3 of top 10)
allClaims.snippet: BrightLocal Business Listings Visibility Study: business directories make up almost a third (31%) of the top ten organic search results overall.

allClaims.claim: NC-specific anchor citation: the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors (NCLBGC) maintains a public license-verification directory (portal.nclbgc.org/Public/Search) covering ~76,160 licensed contractors. A verified NCLBGC profile is a credential-gated, NC-authoritative entity signal — a one-time foundational citation that thin/unlicensed competitors cannot replicate. Pair with the local Chamber of Commerce.
allClaims.stat: NCLBGC public directory of ~76,160 licensed NC contractors; verify-license search at portal.nclbgc.org/Public/Search
allClaims.snippet: NCLBGC 'Verify License Search' / 'Find License Near Me' at portal.nclbgc.org/Public/Search; NC contractor records ~76,160.

allClaims.claim: Local Chamber of Commerce directory listings are typically DoFollow and indexed by Google — a genuine local-trust + low-tier link signal — but priced ~$125/yr (annual, not one-time) and bought as much for networking as for SEO. Honest framing: a modest recurring local-trust citation, NOT a high-equity link; value the referral traffic, don't oversell the link.
allClaims.stat: Chamber listing ~$125/year; chamber directory pages indexed + dofollow per expert investigation
allClaims.snippet: Expert: chamber directory pages are 'indexed by Google' and 'the links also seem to be do-follow'; 'a structured citation from a chamber is worth $125 a year' — but 'you're paying to gain networking access, not just for a link.'

allClaims.claim: BBB is NoFollow and paid (accreditation fee), so its SEO link value is nil — its value is LOCAL TRUST / entity validation, not link equity. Experts explicitly flag it is 'not actually a follow link and isn't cheap.' Sell BBB as a trust badge + citation, never as a backlink.
allClaims.stat: BBB DA 91, NoFollow; accreditation is a paid annual fee
allClaims.snippet: Expert: 'the BBB isn't actually a follow link and isn't cheap either.' BrightLocal table confirms BBB DA 91 NoFollow.

allClaims.claim: Angi and HomeAdvisor are LEAD-GEN MARKETPLACES, not free citations — they carry entity-validation/profile value but the core model is pay-per-lead ($15-$120+/lead, shared among 3-8 contractors, ~$300-$2,500/mo typical spend) with heavy outbound sales pressure. Flag honestly: claim the free profile for citation/entity value; do NOT conflate it with the paid lead product or imply it is a clean SEO citation.
allClaims.stat: Angi/HomeAdvisor: $15-$120+ per shared lead (3-8 contractors), $300-$2,500/mo typical; ~10-15% close rate -> $600-$1,200 CPA
allClaims.snippet: Pay-per-lead model; contractors pay $15-$120+ per homeowner contact, leads shared among 3-8 contractors; $300-$2,500/mo; 'constant calls and false promises from Angi Ads sales team.'

allClaims.claim: Google's March 2020 nofollow change reframed nofollow from a directive to a 'hint' — so high-DA nofollow citations (Yelp, BBB, Houzz) may pass marginal/indirect signal and remain valuable for entity corroboration and referral, but you cannot promise link equity from them. Promise the FLOOR (consistent NAP + AI-feed + possible referral), not a ranking lift.
allClaims.stat: Google reclassified nofollow as a 'hint' (not a directive), March 2020
allClaims.snippet: 'back in March 2020, Google announced that they no longer looked at NoFollow as a directive, and instead a hint.'

allClaims.claim: RANKED FOUNDATIONAL TIER-1 SET (impact-vs-effort, one-time/free first): Tier A (free, DoFollow, AI-relevant) = Google Business Profile, Apple Business Connect, Bing Places, Nextdoor; Tier B (free/freemium, high-DA, NoFollow citation value) = Yelp, Foursquare, Houzz, Yellow Pages; Tier C (paid recurring, trust not equity) = BBB, Chamber of Commerce; Tier D (NC credential anchor, free, defensible) = NCLBGC license profile; FLAG-WITH-CARE = Angi/HomeAdvisor/Thumbtack (lead-gen marketplaces, claim free profile only). Build once, verify NAP, stop.
allClaims.stat: Tier A free+dofollow+AI: GBP/Apple/Bing/Nextdoor; Tier B free high-DA nofollow: Yelp/Foursquare/Houzz/YP; Tier C paid trust: BBB/Chamber; Tier D NC: NCLBGC
allClaims.snippet: Synthesis across BrightLocal DA/follow table + Moz 7% citation weight + Apple/Bing free + NCLBGC directory + Angi/HomeAdvisor pay-per-lead model.

allClaims.claim: The 2026 Whitespark Local Search Ranking Factors report (released Nov 6 2025, the most recent edition) weights citation signals at only 6% for the Local Pack/Maps (6th of 8 factors) and 7% for Local Organic (tied 6th) — confirming citations are table-stakes with low direct ranking weight. This is the single most current, expert-survey primary figure and it cleanly supports the 'build the foundation once, then stop chasing volume' thesis. Promote this over round-1's older Moz/HOTH 7% figure.
allClaims.stat: Citations = 6% Local Pack (6th), 7% Local Organic (tied 6th); top Local Pack factor = Google Business Profile 32%, Reviews 20%, On-Page 15%; top Organic = On-Page 33%, Links 24%
allClaims.snippet: Local Pack/Maps: Citations rank 6th at 6%. Local Organic: Citations rank 6th (tied) at 7%. AI Search Visibility: Citations rank 3rd at 13%. Local Pack top 3: Google Business Profile Signals 32%, Review Signals 20%, On-Page Signals 15%. Local Organic top 3: On-Page 33%, Link Signals 24%, Behavioral 10%.

allClaims.claim: THE STRONGEST AI-VISIBILITY REFRAME: in the same 2026 Whitespark report, citation signals JUMP to 3rd place at 13% for AI-search visibility (vs 6-7% for pack/organic) — and three of the top five AI-visibility factors are citation-related. This is the defensible modern reason to build the tier-1 foundation: not pack rank lift, but feeding the AI/answer-engine layer. Sell citations as an AI-feed + entity play, NOT a backlink or pack-rank play.
allClaims.stat: Citations = 13% / 3rd for AI visibility (vs 6% pack, 7% organic); top AI factors = On-Page 24%, Reviews 16%, Citations 13%
allClaims.snippet: AI Search Visibility: Citations rank 3rd at 13%. ... 'Three of the top five factors for AI are related to citations.' AI Search Visibility top 3: On-Page Signals 24%, Review Signals 16%, Citation Signals 13%.

allClaims.claim: INDEPENDENT, LARGEST-SAMPLE CORROBORATOR (28M+ AI responses): the Foundation Marketing + AirOps Q4-2025 study ranks the exact tier-1 directories in this pillar by AI-citation VOLUME — Yelp 512,680, BBB 149,710, Angi 145,633, Thumbtack 56,004, HomeAdvisor 33,582, Nextdoor 10,308 across ChatGPT/Gemini/Perplexity/Google AI Mode. This is measured (not survey) data and gives a defensible AI-citation-volume ranking of the foundational set. Note it reframes Yelp/BBB/Angi as AI-citation engines even though they pass no link equity (round 1's nofollow finding).
allClaims.stat: Yelp 512,680 AI citations (3.4x BBB) > BBB 149,710 > Angi 145,633 > Thumbtack 56,004 > HomeAdvisor 33,582 > Nextdoor 10,308; dataset 28M+ AI responses / 318M total citations, Q4 2025

allClaims.claim: BrightLocal's independent AI-listings study (20 searches x 10 niches x 4 AI platforms) confirms AI engines pull local answers from the foundational directory set: Yelp cited in 33% of overall searches (every industry on Perplexity), business's OWN website 58% of the time, and Foursquare powering 60-70% of ChatGPT local results. Defensible takeaway: the client's own site + a Yelp/Foursquare/Bing foundation is what AI cites — exactly the one-time tier-1 build, plus reinforces why the deep authority SITE is the spine (own-website = the single most-cited source).
allClaims.stat: Yelp 33% of searches; own business website 58% (ChatGPT, Dec-2024); Foursquare 60-70% of ChatGPT local results; methodology 20 searches x 10 niches x 4 platforms
allClaims.snippet: Yelp was used as a source in 33% of our overall searches. ... ChatGPT used business websites as a source 58% of the time. ... 60% and 70% of local results on ChatGPT come straight from Foursquare's city guide listings.

allClaims.claim: PRIMARY confirmation of the Foursquare->ChatGPT pipeline that justifies prioritizing a Foursquare listing: Foursquare officially announced (Dec 16 2024) it partners with OpenAI on ChatGPT search, its Places API (100M+ POI, 200+ countries) delivering real-world results. This is the first-party source behind round-1's 'ChatGPT pulls from Foursquare' claim — upgrade the citation from inference to Foursquare's own announcement.

allClaims.snippet: Foursquare is proud to partner with @OpenAI on ChatGPT search. Our Places API - with 100M+ POI across 200+ countries - delivers relevant real-world results to user queries.

allClaims.claim: THE EXACT 'BUILD ONCE, STOP' BENCHMARK (defensible scope ceiling for a one-time deliverable): BrightLocal's expert citation survey (22 experts) — 90% say accurate citations matter, but the foundational build is ~35 citations in the first couple months (median 21-30), and building MORE past that has sharply diminishing returns. This is the number to scope the one-time tier-1 citation deliverable to, and the honest reason not to upsell ongoing citation volume.

allClaims.snippet: 90% of the experts in our study report that accurate citations are important to local search ranking. ... The average number of citations to build in the first couple of months is 35, with a median range of 21-30. ... The initial flush of high quality, consistent citations can have a valuable influence on a new business, but continuing to build these at a steady rate doesn't have the same level of impact.

allClaims.claim: AI-citation entry threshold is low and step-function — strengthens the 'one-time build clears the bar' case: SE Ranking found a brand with NO review-platform (e.g. Trustpilot) profile has a ~1% median AI-citation rate, but even a minimal profile (1-13 reviews) jumps to 53.5%; review-platform presence = ~3x higher AI-citation probability. Honest framing: simply EXISTING on the foundational set crosses the AI-visibility threshold — you don't need volume, you need presence. Label as a single-vendor study (SE Ranking), corroborated directionally by the Foundation/AirOps and BrightLocal data above.

pillars.title: Manufacturer / credential backlinks
pillars.section:
## PILLAR L3 — Manufacturer / Credential Backlinks

**Bottom line: a certified roofer's manufacturer profile passes a real dofollow link from a high-authority, topically-perfect domain — and most roofers leave that link slot empty.** This is a one-time, shippable off-page win, not a recurring spend. We confirmed the equity by direct inspection, not by trusting a vendor blog.

**The link is real and it follows (measured, not assumed).** A live GAF Master Elite profile's "Visit Website" anchor points to the contractor's own .com, carries `rel="noopener noreferrer"` with **no nofollow**, and sits in the server-rendered HTML (195,055 bytes, crawlable — not JS-injected) ([gaf.com](https://www.gaf.com/en-us/roofing-contractors/residential/usa/mo/kearney/elite-master-contractors-1119929)). A live Owens Corning profile is even cleaner — the contractor's outbound link carries `rel="(none)"`, a plain follow link, also in server-rendered HTML ([owenscorning.com](https://www.owenscorning.com/en-us/roofing/contractors/contractor-profile/219549)). These two are the load-bearing, measured-dofollow directories.

**CertainTeed is NOT confirmed — do not assume parity.** CertainTeed's Find-a-Pro is a JavaScript SPA with no server-rendered profile anchors exposed; per-profile dofollow is unverified and must be inspected on the specific live profile before we count it ([certainteed.com](https://www.certainteed.com/find-a-pro)). NRCA / association directories are gated dynamic-search (eWeb) — topically relevant but unverified equity, secondary tier ([industry.nrca.net](https://industry.nrca.net/eweb/DynamicPage.aspx?site=nrca&webcode=NRCAMbrDirectory)).

**Dofollow link equity, not just a citation.** The value is three-part: (1) a crawlable follow link feeding Google's links/prominence signal, (2) topical relevance (a roofing manufacturer linking a roofer), and (3) a homeowner referral channel off the directory itself ([localroofingseo.agency](https://www.localroofingseo.agency/blog/link-building-for-roofing-contractors)). We sell it on relevance + confirmed dofollow + referral — never on a borrowed DA/DR number, because Google does not use Moz DA or Ahrefs DR as ranking factors ([thehoth.com](https://www.thehoth.com/blog/da-vs-dr/)). We could not pull a numeric DR (checkers were CAPTCHA-gated); authority is substantiated qualitatively — GAF is the largest North American roofing manufacturer at ~40% share, founded 1886 ([goingwithgibbs.com](https://goingwithgibbs.com/gaf-vs-certainteed-vs-owens-corning-which-manufacturer-certification-matters-most/)).

**The link is credential-gated — qualify the prospect first.** It cannot be manufactured; the client must hold and maintain the cert. GAF Master Elite: <3% (as low as ~2%) of US roofers, requires licensure in good standing, ~$1M insurance, a low-warranty-claim record, and ongoing GAF testing ([goingwithgibbs.com](https://goingwithgibbs.com/gaf-vs-certainteed-vs-owens-corning-which-manufacturer-certification-matters-most/)). OC Platinum Preferred is the scarcest — **invitation-only**, highest satisfaction scores of any OC tier, well under 10% (often cited <1%) ([owenscorning.com](https://www.owenscorning.com/en-us/roofing/contractors/locations)). CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster is craft-gated (~top 1%; 50% of crew + all supervisors credentialed) ([certainteed.com](https://www.certainteed.com/select-shinglemaster)). For an uncertified roofer this pillar is a "get certified, then claim it" roadmap — not an immediate deliverable.

**One-time vs ongoing:** ONE-TIME. The action is completing the profile and pasting in the website link — independent guidance literally says "ensure your profile is complete and consists of a link to your site," and notes many contractors leave it unclaimed ([roofingwebmasters.com](https://www.roofingwebmasters.com/link-building/)). In scope for KM.

**Equity vs citation:** EQUITY (dofollow link) — confirmed for GAF + OC; unconfirmed/citation-at-best for CertainTeed until inspected.

**Approximate one-time cost:** the link itself is $0 marginal — only the labor to complete/verify the profile (the cert dues are a separate, pre-existing business cost the contractor already pays to be certified). No recurring link spend.

**Impact vs effort:** LOW effort, MODERATE-but-FOUNDATIONAL impact. One credential link won't move rankings alone — it's a high-trust base link in a diversified profile plus a referral/E-E-A-T signal. Promote it as the high-floor, low-effort foundation of the link profile, not the lever that wins organic dominance by itself.

**What NOT to oversell:** it's one credential-gated dofollow link — a high-floor foundation + referral channel, not a ranking silver bullet, not a quotable DA/DR score, and CertainTeed/association equity is unverified until the specific profile is inspected.

loadBearing.claim: A live GAF Master Elite contractor profile passes a DOFOLLOW link to the contractor's own website: the 'Visit Website' anchor points to the contractor's external .com, carries rel="noopener noreferrer" with no nofollow, and is present in the server-rendered raw HTML (not JavaScript-injected), so it is fully crawlable and passes real link equity.
loadBearing.stat: rel="noopener noreferrer" (no nofollow); present in 195,055-byte server-rendered HTML; external .com, target=_blank
loadBearing.snippet: Live DOM + raw-HTML inspection (Chrome): 'Visit Website' anchor isExternal:true, tld:com, rel:'noopener noreferrer', hasNofollow:false, target:'_blank'. fetch() returned rawHtmlLength 195055 with visitWebsiteInRawHtml:true; nofollowNearby:false (only nofollow rels on the page were GAF's own corporate/affiliate footer links).
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the entire pillar's foundation — the measured proof that the credential link is a real follow link, not a nofollow citation. The offer claim 'high-authority dofollow link' lives or dies on this. It goes on the slide.

loadBearing.claim: A live Owens Corning contractor profile also passes a DOFOLLOW link to the contractor's website — even cleaner than GAF: the contractor's external link carries rel="(none)" (a plain follow link, no nofollow) and is present in the server-rendered raw HTML.
loadBearing.stat: rel=(none), external .net domain, in 56,080-byte raw HTML; 2 external non-social links, neither nofollow
loadBearing.snippet: Live DOM + raw-HTML inspection (Chrome): externalNonSocialCount:2, sample [{rel:'(none)', tld:'net'},{rel:'(none)', tld:'com'}]; websiteBtns nofollow:false; rawLen 56080, visitWebsiteInRaw:true. No rel=nofollow on the contractor's outbound link.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Second of the two measured-dofollow directories that anchor the pitch. Two independent manufacturers both passing follow links removes the 'lucky single sample' objection. Reel/slide claim.

loadBearing.claim: GAF Master Elite is genuinely scarce and credential-gated: <3% (some sources ~2%) of US roofers qualify, requiring a state license in good standing, ~$1M general-liability + workers'-comp insurance, a documented low-warranty-claim track record, and ongoing GAF testing. The link is earned, not buyable.
loadBearing.stat: <3% (as low as ~2%) of US roofers; ~$1M insurance; ongoing GAF testing
loadBearing.snippet: "GAF Master Elite: Less than 3% of roofing contractors in the United States qualify." Requirements: valid state contractor's license in good standing; general liability + workers' comp insurance; documented positive reviews; low warranty-claim history; pass GAF continuing-education. Corroborated by AKVM/Presidential Exteriors (~$1M insurance, 'as low as 2%').
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The scarcity + qualification bar is what makes the link defensible and a differentiator (not a directory anyone can spam into). It also gates the prospect — must qualify first. Anchors the offer narrative.

loadBearing.claim: The credential-link play is a one-time, shippable off-page win: independent SEO guidance tells roofers simply to 'ensure your profile is complete and consists of a link to your site,' and notes many certified contractors under-utilize the manufacturer 'find a contractor' tools they already qualify for — a claimable-but-unclaimed dofollow link that costs only the effort to complete the profile, not a recurring spend.
loadBearing.stat: one-time profile completion; $0 marginal link cost (labor only)
loadBearing.snippet: "Manufacturers and distributors often run 'find a contractor' tools or spotlight features for certified partners... ensure your profile is complete and consists of a link to your site, which will boost your link building." Implies many leave the link slot empty — the claimable-but-unclaimed gap. (Vendor-incentive source; corroborated by the measured dofollow findings L3-1/L3-2.)
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Defines the deliverable as ONE-TIME and shippable (in scope for KM), which is the offer-structure claim. If this were ongoing/client-managed it would be out of scope. Source is vendor-incentive, so flag for independent corroboration.

loadBearing.claim: CertainTeed Find-a-Pro is a JavaScript SPA, so per-contractor outbound dofollow equity is NOT confirmed and must not be assumed equal to GAF/OC; the directory renders results client-side and exposes no server-rendered profile anchors. Lead the pitch with the two MEASURED-dofollow directories (GAF, OC) and inspect any CertainTeed profile before counting it.
loadBearing.stat: looksLikeSPA:true; 134,610-byte shell; 0 'view profile' anchors exposed
loadBearing.snippet: Live inspection (Chrome): title 'Find A Pro - Home', looksLikeSPA:true, viewProfileButtons:0, profileHrefPatterns:['/credential-contractor-center-us'], rawHasResults:true but results render inside the JS app. The exact 'verify dofollow PER source, do not assume equity' caveat.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the honesty guardrail that keeps the pillar defensible — it prevents the overstatement the brief warns against (claiming all three manufacturers pass equal equity). Stating the limit on the slide is what makes the GAF/OC claims credible.

whatNotToOversell: It is ONE credential-gated dofollow link — a high-floor foundation link + referral/E-E-A-T signal, NOT a ranking silver bullet (per warm Whitespark context links are ~24% of organic weight, and one link won't move rankings alone).

Never quote a DA/DR number for the manufacturer domains — none was pulled from a checker (CAPTCHA-gated), and Google does not use DA/DR as ranking factors; authority is a qualitative proxy (GAF ~40% market share) only.
Do NOT claim CertainTeed passes the same equity as GAF/OC — its Find-a-Pro is a JS SPA and per-profile dofollow is unverified; inspect the specific live profile before counting it.
Do NOT claim NRCA / association directory links pass dofollow equity — the directory is gated eWeb dynamic search, equity unverified; treat as topical/secondary.
The link is credential-GATED — it is not a deliverable for an uncertified roofer; for them it is a 'get certified, then claim it' roadmap, not an immediate win.

Dofollow status is a point-in-time observation — manufacturer profile link slots can be admin-controlled or have nofollow added without notice; re-verify post-completion and on a cadence, don't promise it's permanent.

Do NOT pitch manufacturer directories as the universally-recognized #1 roofer backlink — mainstream guides (e.g. ServiceTitan) omit them entirely; they are a sophisticated under-the-radar differentiator, not an industry-consensus must-have. The seed's 'highest-ROI link' / 'DA 60-80' framing is unsourced extrapolation — drop it.
gaps: No numeric DR/DA pulled for gaf.com / owenscorning.com / certainteed.com — free checkers (Ahrefs, seo.ai) were CAPTCHA/form-gated and I will not solve CAPTCHAs. The 'high-authority' claim rests on qualitative corroboration + GAF's ~40% market share, not a measured DR. A logged-in Ahrefs/Moz read would close this.

CertainTeed: an individual SELECT ShingleMaster contractor PROFILE page (not the SPA results list) was not reached, so the actual outbound-website-link rel attribute and server-render status for CertainTeed remain unconfirmed.
