GAF/OC dofollow status was confirmed on ONE profile each (sample size 1 per manufacturer) — high confidence the template is consistent, but not proven across the full directory; a multi-profile sweep would harden it.

Whether GAF/OC route the outbound link through a tracking redirect that strips equity was checked for GAF (direct external .com, no redirect observed) but not exhaustively for query-string/JS redirect on click.

No NC-specific roofing association with a crawlable, dofollow member directory was located — whether a regional NC chapter or distributor (e.g., ABC Supply / SRS Distribution partner pages) offers a verifiable dofollow link is an open, per-source check.
Referral-traffic magnitude from the manufacturer locators (how many homeowner clicks actually flow to the contractor site) is asserted by sources but not independently quantified.

No numeric Domain Rating (Ahrefs DR) or Domain Authority (Moz DA) for gaf.com / owenscorning.com / certainteed.com could be captured — the free Ahrefs and Moz checkers are JS/CAPTCHA/form-gated and return no number to WebFetch or firecrawl. The 'high-authority domain' claim remains QUALITATIVE only (largest NA manufacturer, ~40% share, national brands). Do NOT assert a specific DA/DR number without a live checker reading; this is the single biggest open data point for the pillar.

Firecrawl was out of credits (HTTP 402) the entire second pass, and GAF/OC block WebFetch (403 anti-bot). Could not independently RE-inspect the live GAF/OC raw HTML in round 2 to confirm the dofollow rel attribute persists in 2026 — relying on round 1's direct inspection. Recommend a one-time re-verification via a headless browser / Claude-in-Chrome before the claim goes FTC-bound in a reel.

CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster Find-a-Pro outbound-link crawlability is STILL unconfirmed (round 1 found it is a JS SPA; round 2 surfaced no new evidence it is server-rendered). Treat CertainTeed equity as unverified until per-profile inspection.

No NC/Triangle-specific data found on how many local (Raleigh/Durham/Cary) roofers hold each cert, nor any NC-specific measurement of organic lift from a manufacturer backlink. All percentages are national/North-American.

No independent measured study quantifying the organic-ranking lift attributable specifically to a manufacturer directory backlink (e.g., before/after referring-domain study). All 'high-value' claims are directional/expert-opinion, not a controlled measurement — promise the FLOOR (a real, relevant, credential-gated dofollow link from a high-authority national domain), never a ranking-delta number.

counter.point: Google does not use Moz DA or Ahrefs DR as direct ranking factors — so 'high-DA manufacturer link' is a correlation proxy, not a guaranteed ranking lever. The mechanism that actually matters is relevance + crawlable follow link feeding Google's own Prominence/links signal, which is why the DOFOLLOW + server-rendered finding (measured) is the load-bearing claim, not any DA number.
counter.soWhat: Sell the link on topical relevance + confirmed dofollow + referral traffic, NOT on a borrowed DA/DR score. Never quote a DA number we did not pull from a checker.

counter.point: A single manufacturer link is one link — per the warm Whitespark context, links carry ~24% of ORGANIC weight but only ~8% of PACK weight, and one credential link won't move rankings alone. Its value is as a high-trust FOUNDATION link in a diversified profile, plus a homeowner referral channel and an E-E-A-T/trust signal — not a silver bullet.
counter.soWhat: Frame credential links as the high-floor, low-effort base of the link profile (one-time, shippable), not as the thing that wins organic dominance by itself.

counter.point: The link is strictly credential-GATED: the client must actually hold GAF Master Elite / OC Platinum Preferred / CertainTeed SELECT. If a target roofer is not certified, this entire pillar is unavailable to them — it is not a link KM can manufacture; it requires the contractor to pass and maintain a real-world certification (insurance, training, track record, and for OC an invitation).
counter.soWhat: Qualify the prospect first. For uncertified roofers, the credential-link play is a 'go get certified, then claim it' roadmap, not an immediate deliverable.

counter.point: CertainTeed Find-a-Pro is a JS SPA — assuming it passes the same equity as GAF/OC would be exactly the overstatement the brief warns against. The contractor's outbound link may be client-rendered (Google can render JS but it's slower/less reliable than server-rendered HTML) or could carry nofollow on the actual profile, which was not reachable to inspect.
counter.soWhat: Do not promise CertainTeed equity sight-unseen; inspect the specific live profile before counting it, and lead the pitch with the two MEASURED-dofollow directories (GAF, OC).

counter.point: Manufacturer profile website-link slots are sometimes optional or admin-controlled, and profiles can be incomplete or out-of-date — the link only exists/passes if the profile is actively completed and kept current, and some directories may add nofollow at any time without notice.
counter.soWhat: The 'one-time shippable' action is real but must be verified post-completion (re-inspect the live rel attribute), and re-checked on a cadence — treat the dofollow status as a point-in-time observation, not permanent.

counter.point: Mainstream 'top roofing directories' guides from major industry platforms do NOT include manufacturer 'find a contractor' directories at all — ServiceTitan's 7-directory list is Google Business Profile, Yelp, Angi, Thumbtack, Houzz, BBB, Nextdoor, plus paid aggregators. Manufacturer/credential directories are absent.
counter.soWhat: Cuts both ways: it independently supports our 'underutilized / contractors miss it' thesis (even the big guides overlook it), but it also means manufacturer directories are NOT industry-consensus 'must-have' links — don't pitch them as the universally-recognized #1 roofer backlink. They are a sophisticated, under-the-radar play, which is exactly why they're a differentiator but not a slam-dunk everyone-already-knows.

counter.point: 2026 SEO consensus is that directory backlinks only help when they are dofollow, relevant, indexed, and from reputable sources — mass/thin/nofollow directory links have diminishing returns and can look manipulative. Nofollow directory links drive referral traffic and brand signals but 'don't pass ranking authority.'
counter.soWhat: Our pillar SURVIVES this skeptic test precisely because round 1 directly inspected the raw HTML and found GAF + Owens Corning are dofollow, server-rendered, topically relevant, and on high-authority domains — the exact profile that still works in 2026. The counter-evidence kills the generic 'submit to 200 directories' play, not the credential-gated manufacturer link. Keep the claim narrow to the verified-dofollow manufacturer profiles; do not bundle it with bulk directory submission.

counter.point: No source (manufacturer-side or independent) frames the certified-contractor directory listing as a BACKLINK/SEO benefit — they market it purely as a homeowner-trust / warranty-eligibility / lead-referral feature. The SEO link equity is a byproduct, not a stated program benefit.
counter.soWhat: Reinforces that the dofollow-link value is something WE identified via direct HTML inspection, not something the manufacturer advertises — a genuine edge, but it also means the 'this is a known high-ROI SEO link' framing has no manufacturer-first-party backing. Anchor the claim on the inspected HTML (measured), not on any program marketing.

allClaims.claim: GAF contractor profile pages pass a DOFOLLOW link to the contractor's own website. On a live Master Elite profile, the contractor 'Visit Website' anchor points to the contractor's external .com domain and carries rel="noopener noreferrer" — NO nofollow — and it is present in the server-rendered raw HTML (not JavaScript-injected), so it is fully crawlable and passes real link equity.
allClaims.stat: rel="noopener noreferrer" (no nofollow); present in 195,055-byte server-rendered HTML; 1 external 'Visit Website' anchor, target=_blank, external .com
allClaims.snippet: Live DOM + raw-HTML inspection (Chrome): the 'Visit Website' anchor — isExternal:true, tld:com, rel:'noopener noreferrer', hasNofollow:false, target:'_blank'. fetch() of the page returned rawHtmlLength 195055 with visitWebsiteInRawHtml:true and the matched 'rel="noopener noreferrer"' in the snippet window, nofollowNearby:false (the only nofollow rels on the page were GAF's own corporate/affiliate footer links e.g. Standard Industries).

allClaims.claim: Owens Corning contractor profile pages also pass a DOFOLLOW link to the contractor's own website — even cleaner than GAF. On a live OC contractor profile the contractor's external website link (a .net domain) carries rel="(none)" (a plain follow link, no nofollow) and the website link is present in the server-rendered raw HTML.
allClaims.stat: rel=(none), external .net domain, in 56,080-byte raw HTML; only 2 external non-social links and neither nofollow
allClaims.snippet: Live DOM + raw-HTML inspection (Chrome): externalNonSocialCount:2, sample [{rel:'(none)', tld:'net', label:'https://certifiedroofings...'},{rel:'(none)', tld:'com', label:'click here'}]; websiteBtns nofollow:false; rawLen 56080, visitWebsiteInRaw:true. No rel=nofollow on the contractor's outbound link.

allClaims.claim: CertainTeed's Find-a-Pro is a JavaScript single-page app (SPA), so per-contractor outbound website-link crawlability is NOT confirmed and should NOT be assumed equal to GAF/OC. The directory renders results client-side and exposes no standard server-rendered contractor-profile anchors; do not claim CertainTeed passes the same dofollow equity without per-profile verification.
allClaims.stat: looksLikeSPA:true; 134,610-byte shell; 0 'view profile' anchors exposed; only internal href pattern surfaced was /credential-contractor-center-us
allClaims.snippet: Live inspection (Chrome): title 'Find A Pro - Home', looksLikeSPA:true, viewProfileButtons:0, profileHrefPatterns:['/credential-contractor-center-us'], rawHasResults:true but results render inside the JS app. This is the exact 'some locators are JS-rendered — verify dofollow PER source, do not assume equity' caveat.

allClaims.claim: Manufacturer find-a-contractor directories are independently described as among the most valuable roofer backlinks specifically because they sit on established, high-authority domains and also drive direct referral traffic from homeowners — i.e. relevance + authority + a conversion channel, not just a link. They are a 'complete-your-profile' link the certified contractor controls.
allClaims.stat: n/a (qualitative)
allClaims.snippet: "Roofing material manufacturers like GAF, Owens Corning, and CertainTeed maintain certified contractor directories that include backlinks." / "These backlinks are highly valuable because they come from established, high-authority domains and also deliver direct referral traffic from homeowners seeking trusted contractors." (roofing SEO agency blog — vendor-incentive, but the claim is corroborated by the measured dofollow finding above.)

allClaims.claim: SEED CORRECTION: the seed library framed manufacturer find-a-pro as literally the single 'highest-ROI link' for a roofer, but the underlying source (localroofingseo.agency) lists it as ONE of eight link-building tactics and does NOT rank it #1, does NOT cite a DA number, and does NOT state dofollow/nofollow. The 'highest-ROI' / DA-60-80 framing is an internal extrapolation, not a quotable source claim — promise the floor (a real, relevant, credential-gated dofollow link as confirmed by direct inspection), not the unsourced superlative.
allClaims.stat: 1 of 8 listed tactics; no DA figure; no dofollow/nofollow stated in source
allClaims.snippet: Fetch of the source confirmed: 'The article lists this tactic as one of eight link-building strategies but does not claim it as superior to others or provide technical link specifications for manufacturer directories.' No DA number and no dofollow/nofollow attribute is stated.

allClaims.claim: GAF Master Elite is the credential gate for the GAF link and is genuinely scarce: less than 3% (some sources ~2%) of U.S. roofing contractors hold it. Requirements include a valid state license in good standing, adequate general-liability + workers'-comp insurance (commonly cited ~$1M), a documented quality/low-warranty-claim track record, and ongoing GAF training/testing. This is the 'qualify-but-must-hold-the-cert' bar — the link is not buyable, only earned.
allClaims.stat: <3% (as low as ~2%) of US roofers; ~$1M insurance; ongoing GAF testing
allClaims.snippet: "GAF Master Elite: Less than 3% of roofing contractors in the United States qualify." Requirements quoted: valid state contractor's license in good standing; general liability + workers' comp insurance; documented positive reviews; history of low warranty claims; pass GAF continuing-education. Corroborated by AKVM/Presidential Exteriors ("~$1 million" insurance, 'less than 3%, as low as 2%').

allClaims.claim: CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster is the highest CertainTeed tier (~top 1% of CertainTeed contractors / <10% qualify) and is craft-gated: SARP/Master Craftsman training for crew (commonly cited as 50% of the install crew plus all supervisors credentialed), minimum insurance, a manufacturer track record, and ongoing compliance — lose the standards, lose the designation.
allClaims.stat: SELECT = top ~1% of CertainTeed contractors / <10% qualify; 50% of crew + all supervisors credentialed
allClaims.snippet: CertainTeed primary credential page for SELECT ShingleMaster. Corroborated by econo-roofing and Gibbs: 'To qualify for SELECT ShingleMaster, contractors must ensure 50% of their shingle installation crew, plus all job supervisors, are credentialed as a Master Craftsman'; Gibbs: SELECT 'Less than 10%' qualify; 'contractors who don't meet the standards lose the designation.'

allClaims.claim: Owens Corning Platinum Preferred is the scarcest and most exclusive of the three: it is INVITATION-ONLY (a contractor cannot self-apply), requires the highest customer-satisfaction scores of any OC tier and ongoing training/evaluation, and is held by well under 10% (often cited under 1%) of US roofers. Combined with the confirmed dofollow OC link, it is the highest-bar credential link of the set.
allClaims.stat: invitation-only; <10% (often cited <1%) of US roofers
allClaims.snippet: OC primary contractor pages describe Platinum Preferred as 'the top tier of Owens Corning's exclusive network.' Corroborated: 'The Owens Corning Platinum Preferred program is invitation-only — contractors cannot apply for it' and 'requires the highest customer satisfaction scores of any tier'; Gibbs lists Platinum 'Less than 10%' qualify.

allClaims.claim: The 'qualify-but-never-claim' gap is real and is a one-time, shippable off-page win: independent SEO guidance explicitly tells roofers the action is simply to 'ensure your profile is complete and consists of a link to your site,' and that many contractors under-utilize the manufacturer/distributor 'find a contractor' tools they already qualify for. For a certified roofer this is a high-authority, topically-relevant dofollow link that costs only the effort to complete the profile — not a recurring spend.
allClaims.stat: n/a (one-time profile completion)
allClaims.snippet: "Manufacturers and distributors often run 'find a contractor' tools or spotlight features for certified partners... To secure these links, contractors must keep profiles updated... ensure your profile is complete and consists of a link to your site, which will boost your link building." Implies many leave the link slot empty — the claimable-but-unclaimed gap.

allClaims.claim: Authority proxy for the manufacturer domains: GAF is the largest North-American roofing manufacturer (~40% market share, founded 1886), and GAF/OC/CertainTeed are the three dominant national shingle brands. This substantiates 'high-authority domain' qualitatively even though a specific DR/DA score could not be pulled (free DR checkers were CAPTCHA/form-gated). Do NOT assert a numeric DA of 60-80 without a checker reading.
allClaims.stat: GAF ~40% North American market share; founded 1886
allClaims.snippet: "GAF has been around since 1886 and currently holds about 40% of the North American roofing market"; the three are described as dominating the market 'for good reason: they've established reputations for quality through decades of performance.' (Used as an authority proxy — a precise DR number remains a gap.)

allClaims.claim: National/state roofing associations (NRCA and chapter affiliates) are a SECONDARY, lower-certainty credential-link tier: the NRCA member directory is served through a gated eWeb dynamic search (industry.nrca.net), so member website links are not reliably crawlable/dofollow the way GAF/OC profiles are; and a distinct 'NCRCA' North Carolina body did not surface as a separate searchable directory (NC roofers appear to affiliate via national NRCA). Treat association links as topical but unverified-equity until checked per-directory.
allClaims.stat: NRCA directory = gated eWeb search; no distinct crawlable NCRCA directory found
allClaims.snippet: NRCA member directory is an eWeb DynamicPage search (industry.nrca.net). Search did 'not return a specific website for a separate North Carolina Roofing Contractors Association (NCRCA) member directory... North Carolina roofing contractors are affiliated through the national NRCA.' Equity is unverified — do not assume dofollow.

allClaims.claim: RANKED credential-backlink shortlist by VERIFIED real equity + topical relevance + qualification bar (relevance > raw DA): (1) GAF Master Elite locator — measured DOFOLLOW, server-rendered, scarcest-but-attainable cert, largest manufacturer; (2) Owens Corning Platinum Preferred profile — measured DOFOLLOW (cleanest rel), highest exclusivity (invitation-only); (3) CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster Find-a-Pro — topically relevant + scarce cert, but SPA/JS-rendered so equity UNCONFIRMED — verify the specific profile before promising; (4) NRCA / association directories — topical but gated/unverified equity, secondary.
allClaims.stat: Tier 1: GAF + OC (measured dofollow); Tier 2: CertainTeed (JS, unverified); Tier 3: associations (gated, unverified)
allClaims.snippet: Ranking is the synthesis of the four measured/inspected directory findings above: GAF and OC contractor links were directly observed as dofollow + server-rendered; CertainTeed Find-a-Pro observed as a JS SPA (equity unconfirmed); NRCA observed as a gated eWeb search. GAF maintains a public 'verify factory-certified' page confirming the locator is the canonical verification surface.

allClaims.claim: Independent corroboration (non-manufacturer, third-party roofing-SEO source) that supplier/manufacturer 'find a contractor' directories pass DOFOLLOW links on partner listings — matching round 1's direct raw-HTML inspection of GAF and Owens Corning. A backlink-source comparison table classifies 'Supplier/Manufacturer Directories' as 'Do-follow on partner listings' with the trust signal 'Industry relevance and co-branding,' and explicitly ranks them among the strongest link types.
allClaims.stat: Link type: 'Do-follow on partner listings'; trust signal: 'Industry relevance and co-branding'
allClaims.snippet: Supplier/Manufacturer Directories — Trust Signal: 'Industry relevance and co-branding'; Link Type: 'Do-follow on partner listings'. 'This comparison shows that not all directories are equal: prioritize editorially controlled local outlets and supplier/manufacturer listings for stronger backlink value and long-term trust benefits.'

allClaims.claim: Independent corroboration of the credential-scarcity ranking across all three manufacturer tiers in one source: GAF Master Elite ~2% of US roofers, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster ~1%, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred 'only a small fraction qualify.' This matches round 1's per-cert numbers and confirms the qualification bar is real (licensing, insurance, experience, annual re-certification).
allClaims.stat: GAF Master Elite ~2%; CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster ~1%; OC Platinum Preferred = small fraction
allClaims.snippet: GAF Master Elite: 'Only about 2% of roofers in the US hold this certification.' CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster: 'Only about 1% of roofers hold it.' Owens Corning Platinum Preferred: 'Only a small fraction of their contractors qualify.' Requirements include licensing, insurance, years in business, customer satisfaction ratings, and annual re-certification.

allClaims.claim: Owens Corning Platinum Preferred is confirmed INVITATION-ONLY (cannot self-apply) by an independent contractor source, with a concrete, verified qualification bar: strong BBB rating, state licensing, workers'-comp compliance, minimum $1M general-liability insurance, financial-stability screening, and at least 3 years in business under the same ownership. An OC Area Sales Manager nominates only after demonstrated network performance. This hardens round 1's 'invitation-only, highest-bar credential link' framing with specific requirements.
allClaims.stat: Invitation-only; min $1M GL insurance; 3+ years same ownership; ASM nomination
allClaims.snippet: Platinum Preferred isn't a registration you fill out online or a fee you pay to unlock. It's an invitation-only designation. ... a strong Better Business Bureau rating, proper state licensing, workers' compensation compliance, a minimum of $1 million in general liability insurance, financial stability screening, and at least three years in business under the same ownership.

allClaims.claim: Second independent corroboration of the 'qualify-but-never-claim' gap (the one-time shippable win): manufacturer/distributor 'find a contractor' tools are described as a HIGH-AUTHORITY, referral-driving backlink that many contractors UNDER-utilize by not completing their profiles. The action is simply to keep the profile updated and supply a short project story with photos — effort, not recurring spend.
allClaims.stat: Action = complete/update profile + supply project story; cost = effort only
allClaims.snippet: Manufacturers and distributors often run 'find a contractor' tools or spotlight features for certified partners. These backlinks are highly valuable because they come from established, high-authority domains. They also deliver direct referral traffic from homeowners seeking trusted contractors. To secure these links, contractors must keep profiles updated and provide materials that manufacturers can publish. A short project story with photos is often enough to earn a feature.

allClaims.claim: GAF Master Elite is re-confirmed as ~2% of North American roofers with a $1M-insurance + licensing + annual-recertification bar, from multiple independent 2025 sources — and is explicitly valid for only ONE YEAR, meaning the credential (and thus the link entitlement) must be continuously re-earned. This strengthens the 'not buyable, only earned, and perishable' framing.
allClaims.stat: ~2% of NA roofers; $1M liability insurance; certification valid 1 year (annual renewal)
allClaims.snippet: Only the top 2% of roofing contractors in North America have achieved GAF Master Elite status. Eligibility includes being properly licensed (where required) and carrying at least $1 million in liability insurance plus workers' compensation coverage. GAF's Master Elite certifications are only valid for one year, meaning contractors must regularly prove their qualifications to retain the designation.

pillars.title: On-site local-proof layer (what WE build)
pillars.section:
## PILLAR L4 — On-Site Local-Proof Layer (What We Build)

**Bottom line: the on-site layer does not win the map pack. It makes you eligible and it drives organic location-query visibility.** Sell it on what it actually does, not on rank.

Google attributes the pack's link and review signals to off-site sources, not to your markup ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en)). In the 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors survey, on-page/website signals carry roughly 15% of local-pack weight — third lever, behind Google Business Profile (~32%) and reviews (~20%) ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/google-local-algorithm-and-ranking-factors/)). So the schema/NAP/map layer is the third lever for the pack and a real organic lever — never the pack-ranking driver.

**Schema is entity hygiene, not a ranking boost.** Google's John Mueller is on record that structured data is not a direct ranking factor — "it doesn't mean that we would show it to more users or that it would rank better" ([searchenginejournal.com](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/ranking-factors/schema-markup-ranking/)). `sameAs` declares your business is the same entity as records at external URLs, which is how Google reconciles you into the Knowledge Graph — entity clarity, not a multiplier ([willscott.me](https://willscott.me/2025/07/30/sameas-versus-knowsabout-in-schema/)). A connected `@graph` keyed by `@id` (LocalBusiness, location nodes, services, breadcrumbs referencing each other) is the correct structure for machine reconciliation, and `LocalBusiness` carries `geo`, `areaServed`, and `PostalAddress` to declare served geography from one config block ([schema.org](https://schema.org/LocalBusiness)). The cause→effect: lock the entity, become legible and eligible, then organic depth moves position.

**What the entity layer buys is eligibility, which precedes ranking.** Entity resolution runs before content retrieval in both classic and AI retrieval — a brand that fails recognition is excluded before scoring begins ([organikpi.com](https://organikpi.com/blog/technical-seo/schema-sameas-entity-disambiguation-ai-citations/), vendor-incentive, modeled). That reframes the layer as table-stakes to be in the consideration set, especially as AI-cited URLs increasingly fall outside the organic top-10.

**The measured organic payoff is location-query visibility, not pack position.** An independent 85-day controlled test (11 test / 4 control pages) using `spatialCoverage`/`audience` plus `sameAs` to link locations to Wikipedia/Wikidata/Google KG produced +46% impressions and +42% clicks on non-branded location queries ([schemaapp.com](https://www.schemaapp.com/schema-markup/measurable-impact-of-scaling-entity-linking-for-entity-disambiguation/), vendor-incentive, measured). Floor: a single small vendor experiment on organic impressions/clicks. Ceiling: directional evidence that config-driven geo entity-linking moves location-query visibility. It is not a pack-ranking or lead-volume number — never relabel it as one.

**The GBP landing-page target is a config choice, not a default.** Sterling Sky's controlled test confirms the URL you link from the GBP impacts pack ranking for that page's queries ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/does-the-url-you-link-to-in-google-my-business-impact-ranking-in-the-local-pack/)). But their own default for a single-location business is the homepage (most authority), and post-2025 Diversity Update, pointing the GBP at your already-top-ranking page can hurt. So: single-location flagship → homepage; multi-location / practitioner / non-ranking page → a dedicated NAP-matched city/service page that lists all services to trigger "website mentions" justifications ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/google-business-profile-landing-pages/)). Either way the page must be deep — Sterling Sky's 8,186-business / 200-city study found a slight positive correlation between more substantive words on the linked page and better local rankings, and a negative correlation for hiding the address ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/what-gets-you-ranking-for-near-me-2025/)). This is the anti-doorway build rule: deep real content per location beats thin city pages.

**NAP: claim the mechanism, not a number.** A single config-driven NAP source-of-truth rendered identically in schema, footer, and contact page — matching the GBP and every citation — is the build spec. Consistency matters more than volume; inconsistency confuses entity resolution ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/what-is-nap/), vendor-incentive). The circulating "40% lift / 156% Maps visibility / 27% drop" figures trace to no primary study — do not put a NAP percentage in the reel.

**Map embeds are trust/UX, not ranking.** Embed one real map on the contact/location page for NAP confirmation, lazy-loaded for Core Web Vitals (page speed is a ranking factor). Do not spin up hundreds of map-embed geo pages — Google cracked down on that in 2018 ([gobluemedia.com](https://www.gobluemedia.com/blog/google-maps-seo-rankings/)).

### Lever economics
- **One-time vs ongoing:** This pillar is **100% one-time, shippable** — `@graph`/`sameAs`/`LocalBusiness` schema, the NAP source-of-truth, the lazy-loaded map, and the deep city/service landing pages all ship at build and persist with zero monthly labor. Ongoing client-managed off-page (citations upkeep, review velocity) is out of scope here.
- **Equity vs citation / dofollow vs nofollow:** Not applicable as a backlink lever — the on-site layer creates **no external link equity**. `sameAs` is an entity-reconciliation declaration (citation-class identity signal), not a dofollow backlink. Treat it as entity plumbing, not link building. (No PBN, no link schemes, no gray-hat — excluded by design.)
- **Approximate one-time cost:** Low. It is config + template work driven off one GEOGRAPHY/BUSINESS block — schema and NAP are near-free once the template carries them; the cost is writing genuinely deep per-location content (the anti-doorway tax), not the markup.
- **Impact vs effort:** **Low effort, foundational impact — but bounded.** High leverage as the eligibility floor (you become legible to pack, organic, and AI retrieval) and a modest, measured organic-visibility lever. Low leverage as a direct pack-rank mover (~15% of pack weight, and Google credits the link/review portion off-site). Build it because it is cheap, one-time, and table-stakes — not because it ranks you.

### What NOT to oversell
- Never claim schema/`sameAs`/`@graph` "ranks you higher" — Mueller: no ranking boost. It locks the entity and makes you eligible.
- Never claim the on-site layer wins the 3-pack. The pack is won off-site (GBP ~32% + review velocity ~20%); on-page is ~15% and the link/review share is credited off-site.
- Never put a NAP-consistency percentage (40%/156%/27%) in a reel — no primary source.
- Never relabel the 46%/42% organic-impressions lift as a pack-ranking or lead-volume guarantee; it is one small vendor test on organic location-query visibility.
- Never hard-code "dedicated city page per GBP" as the default — single-location flagships link the homepage.
- Never imply a map embed ranks you; ship it lazy-loaded for trust only.

loadBearing.claim: Google attributes the local-pack prominence signals (links, reviews) to off-site sources, and the on-site/website signal carries only ~15% of pack weight in the 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors survey (behind GBP ~32% and reviews ~20%) — so the on-site layer is necessary but is not the pack-ranking driver.
loadBearing.stat: On-page ~15% of pack weight; GBP ~32%; reviews ~20%
loadBearing.snippet: Google Business Profile (32%) ... Reviews (20%) ... On-page (15%)
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the cardinal honesty anchor of L4: it defines the lever's true weight and stops the offer from selling on-site proof as the thing that wins the pack. Corroborated by Google's own help doc crediting links/reviews off-site.

loadBearing.claim: Schema/structured data is NOT a direct ranking factor — Google's John Mueller stated it 'doesn't mean that we would show it to more users or that it would rank better.' The entity layer's value is eligibility and machine-legibility, not rank.
loadBearing.stat: Schema = no direct ranking boost (Google/Mueller)
loadBearing.snippet: it doesn't mean that we would show it to more users or that it would rank better.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Prevents the single most dangerous FTC-exposed claim — 'our schema ranks you higher.' First-party Google attribution. This line governs how every schema deliverable is framed in reels.

loadBearing.claim: An independent 85-day controlled experiment (11 test / 4 control pages) using place-based entity linking (spatialCoverage/audience + sameAs to Wikipedia/Wikidata/Google KG) produced +46% impressions and +42% clicks for non-branded location queries — the buildable, config-driven organic-visibility payoff of the on-site geo entity layer (organic location-query visibility, NOT pack position or leads).
loadBearing.stat: +46% impressions, +42% clicks on non-branded location queries; 85 days; 11 test / 4 control
loadBearing.snippet: a 46% increase in impressions and a 42% increase in clicks for non-branded queries.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The strongest MEASURED upside number for the pillar — the one quantified payoff worth putting on a slide. Must ship with its floor caveat (single small vendor test, organic-visibility only) attached or it becomes a fabricated guarantee.

loadBearing.claim: The URL linked from the Google Business Profile measurably impacts pack ranking for that page's queries, BUT the correct target is a config choice: single-location businesses should link the homepage (most authority), and post-2025 Diversity Update linking the already-top-ranking page can hurt — dedicated NAP-matched city/service pages are for multi-location/practitioner cases or non-ranking pages.
loadBearing.stat: GBP landing-URL content impacts pack ranking for that page's queries (measured); homepage is the single-location default
loadBearing.snippet: The content on the specific URL you link to is important and impacts ranking in the local results ... linking to the highest-ranking organic page can now hurt rankings due to Google's Diversity Update.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Validates the dedicated-landing-page build pattern AND prevents hard-coding the wrong default into the product. The 'config choice not blanket rule' framing is load-bearing for both honesty and correct delivery.

loadBearing.claim: Deeper location landing pages outperform thin ones: Sterling Sky's 8,186-business / 200-city near-me study found a slight positive correlation between more substantive words on the linked page and better local rankings, and a negative correlation for hiding the address — independent, large-N support for the anti-doorway 'deep real content per location' build rule.
loadBearing.stat: 8,186 businesses / 200 cities; slight positive correlation between substantive page words and local rankings
loadBearing.snippet: a slight correlation between having more substantive words on your page and better local rankings ... 'Is Service Area Business' showed a negative correlation to ranking.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Large-N independent evidence that justifies the anti-doorway depth tax (deep per-location content over thin city pages) — the build discipline that keeps the offer defensible. Note it is a 'slight' correlation; do not inflate.

whatNotToOversell: Never claim schema/sameAs/@graph 'ranks you higher' — Google/Mueller: no direct ranking boost. Frame it as entity-locking + eligibility only.
Never claim the on-site layer wins the 3-pack. Pack is won off-site (GBP ~32% + reviews ~20%); on-page is ~15% and Google credits the link/review portion off-site.

Never put a NAP-consistency percentage (the circulating 40% / 156% / 27% figures) in a reel or pitch — none trace to a primary measured study. Claim the mechanism (consistency > volume), not a number.
Never relabel the 46%/42% Schema App lift as a pack-ranking or lead-volume guarantee — it is one small (11/4) vendor experiment measuring organic location-query impressions/clicks only.
Never hard-code 'a dedicated city page per GBP' as the default — single-location flagships should link the homepage; dedicated pages are for multi-location/practitioner/non-ranking cases.
Never imply an embedded map ranks you; it is UX/trust only and must be lazy-loaded so it doesn't hurt Core Web Vitals (a real ranking factor).

Never sell entity resolution / sameAs as a ranking multiplier — it is a gatekeeping/eligibility prerequisite (table-stakes to be in the consideration set), and the supporting figure is modeled/vendor-sourced.
No PBN / link schemes / gray-hat — the on-site layer creates no external link equity and must not be positioned as link building.
gaps: No primary, traceable study quantifying NAP-consistency's isolated pack-ranking lift — the circulating 40%/156%/27% figures lack methodology. A defensible number would require a BrightLocal/Whitespark/Sterling Sky controlled study; treat as mechanism-only until found.

Google's fuller historical prominence wording ('position in web results is a factor, SEO best practices apply ... links, articles, and directories') is now TRIMMED on the live help page; only secondary sources quote the older version. The first-party citation is weaker than ideal — would want a Wayback/archived snapshot of the prior support.google.com page to anchor it primary.

No isolated experiment separating the ranking effect of schema sameAs/@graph from the confounded content and link changes that usually ship alongside it — entity-linking impact remains directional/confounded, not cleanly causal.

Limited evidence on driving-directions / 'Get Directions' on-site widgets specifically (as opposed to a static map embed) affecting either conversion or ranking — treated here under the same UX/trust framing as the map embed.

Magnitude of the on-site entity layer's contribution to AI/LLM citation eligibility (the OrganiKPI gatekeeping claim) is modeled from one study; no second independent corroborator on the ~77%-outside-top-10 figure.

No raw Whitespark 2026 primary-source capture: the percentages (19% pack / 24% AI) and the '#1 Local Organic / #2 AI Visibility for Dedicated Page per Service' ranking are all via secondary reporters (replyonthefly, harmo, koanthic) because whitespark.ca renders client-side and koanthic 403'd. Need a Firecrawl/JS-render scrape of the Whitespark report (or its PDF) to lock these as primary before reel-binding.

No NC/Triangle-specific or roofing-specific CONTROLLED on-site experiment — only an agency case study (kodescape, vendor-incentive, no isolated variable) corroborates the roofing vertical. The Sterling Sky / Schema App experiments (round 1) remain the only controlled MEASURED evidence and neither is roofing.

The exact ranked list of buildable on-site components by weight (beyond 'dedicated page per service' #1) is not captured verbatim — secondary sources list LocalBusiness schema, location title tags, NAP, internal linking, content depth qualitatively but without ordinal positions. Need the full Whitespark on-site sub-factor table.

No measured isolation of the @graph/sameAs entity layer's contribution SEPARATE from content depth — round 1's Schema App 46%/42% study bundles entity-linking with spatialCoverage content; no study isolates JSON-LD-alone lift (consistent with Mueller's 'not a ranking factor' — likely unmeasurable in isolation, which is itself the honest answer).

Behavioral/engagement signals (clicks, calls, direction requests) are rising in the 2026 study but the on-site mechanisms that drive them (click-to-call, embedded directions) were not quantified this pass.

counter.point: On-site local-proof alone does NOT move the local pack in any large way. Google attributes prominence's link/review signals to OFF-site sources; the LSRF-style breakdowns put on-page at only ~15% of pack weight (vs GBP 32% / reviews 20%). The schema/map/NAP layer is necessary entity hygiene and a real ORGANIC lever, but selling it as a pack-ranking driver overstates it.
counter.soWhat: Position the on-site layer honestly as (a) the entity-locking + eligibility foundation and (b) a genuine ORGANIC-visibility driver (the 46%/42% location-query lift), NOT as the thing that wins the 3-pack. The pack is won off-site (GBP + review velocity) — center organic dominance, treat the pack as the proximity-capped byproduct.

counter.point: Sterling Sky's own default guidance contradicts the naive 'always link GBP to a dedicated city page' rule: for a single-location business the HOMEPAGE usually wins (more authority/backlinks), and post-2025 Diversity Update, pointing the GBP at your already-top-ranking page can HURT.
counter.soWhat: Make the GBP-link target a CONFIG CHOICE keyed to listing count + current rankings, not a blanket 'dedicated landing per GBP.' Single-location flagship: homepage. Multi-location / practitioner / non-ranking page: dedicated NAP-matched city/service page. Don't hard-code the wrong default into the product.

counter.point: sameAs and embedded maps are routinely oversold as ranking levers. sameAs is entity CLARITY (helps Google know which business you are); the embedded map is UX/trust and can actively hurt CWV/page-speed (a real ranking factor) if not lazy-loaded. Neither is a ranking multiplier.
counter.soWhat: Claim sameAs/@graph as 'locks the entity so you're eligible and machine-readable' (true) — never as 'boosts your ranking.' Ship the map lazy-loaded on contact/location pages only. The FTC-exposed reel must not imply a map embed or sameAs string ranks you.

counter.point: The most-cited NAP impact stats ('40% pack-appearance lift', '156% Maps visibility in 90 days', '27% visibility drop') do not trace to a primary measured study — they recur across agency/vendor blogs with no methodology. The seed's '~40% pack-appearance lift' could not be verified to a primary source.
counter.soWhat: Do NOT put a NAP-consistency percentage in the reel. Claim the MECHANISM (consistency > volume; inconsistency confuses entity resolution and can suppress eligibility) and the buildable spec (single NAP source-of-truth across schema/footer/contact matching GBP), not a fabricated number.

counter.point: The strongest measured on-site win (Schema App 46%/42%) is a single small (11 test / 4 control) VENDOR experiment, and it measured ORGANIC location-query impressions/clicks — not local-pack position or revenue.
counter.soWhat: Cite it as a directional/illustrative measured datapoint for the ORGANIC geo-visibility lift with the floor framed conservatively (single small vendor test), and never relabel an organic-impressions lift as a pack-ranking or lead-volume guarantee.

counter.point: Schema/structured data is NOT a direct ranking factor — Google (Mueller) on record calling it 'a very very small thing' and 'no ranking boost.' The entity layer's value is eligibility + machine-legibility, not rank.
counter.soWhat: Reels/pitch must never claim 'schema ranks you higher.' Frame the @graph/sameAs/LocalBusiness layer as entity-clarity and AI/SERP eligibility — the FLOOR (you become legible/eligible), with organic depth as the lever that actually moves position. This is the cardinal honesty line for L4.

counter.point: On-site/website signals are only ~19% of LOCAL-PACK weight (Whitespark 2026); proximity ~55% and GBP ~32% dominate the pack. The on-site layer cannot be sold as the pack-winning lever.
counter.soWhat: Reinforces the locked doctrine: do NOT center the pack. The on-site layer's real prize is ORGANIC regional dominance + AI visibility (where on-page jumps to ~24% and 'dedicated page per service' is #1/#2), which the pack's proximity cap can never deliver. Sell the bigger prize.

counter.point: More location/city pages is a NET LIABILITY when thin — template-swapped city pages 'saw widespread demotions' post-2024 core update and land in 'Crawled – not indexed.' Volume is the trap, not the win.
counter.soWhat: Hard-codes the anti-doorway BLOCKING gate (real-job→page, delete-the-city-name test). The productization spec must cap pages to those backed by genuine local proof; a 300-page spine only helps if every page survives the doorway line. Quality of the on-site proof layer, not page count, is the defensible claim.

counter.point: Google explicitly did NOT confirm it uses structured data to power AI Overviews/Gemini ranking; the AI-visibility weighting for on-page is from an expert-opinion survey (modeled), and the exact 24% figure came from a snippet of a source (koanthic) that 403'd on direct fetch.
counter.soWhat: The 'on-site wins the AI surface' thesis is directionally strong (Whitespark expert consensus + Google reaffirming schema's value) but is MODELED, not measured. Project the AI-visibility ceiling as a trend, promise the organic-depth floor. Confirm the 24% against the Whitespark primary PDF before any reel binds it.

allClaims.claim: Google's own Business Profile Help defines local-pack Prominence as based partly on 'how many websites link to your business' — meaning a business's web/link footprint (which on-site schema and content help establish) feeds the pack. This is the first-party hook that ties an on-site authority layer to local ranking, but Google attributes the link/review signals to off-site, not the on-site markup itself.
allClaims.stat: Prominence is one of 3 primary local ranking factors (relevance, distance, prominence)
allClaims.snippet: Prominence means how well-known a business is. Prominent places are more likely to show up in search results. This factor's also based on info like how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have. More reviews and positive ratings can help your business's local ranking.

allClaims.claim: An earlier/wider version of the same Google Prominence documentation explicitly stated that a business's organic web position is itself a pack factor and that SEO best practices apply — 'Your position in web results is also a factor, so search engine optimization (SEO) best practices apply' and prominence draws on 'links, articles, and directories.' This is the load-bearing first-party statement that organic strength feeds the pack; flag that the LIVE page has since been trimmed to a shorter wording.
allClaims.stat: organic web position = a stated pack prominence factor
allClaims.snippet: Local results are based primarily on relevance, distance, and prominence. [SEJ documents Google's prominence wording that a business's position in web results is a factor and SEO best practices apply; the prominence factor draws on links, articles, and directories.]

allClaims.claim: schema.org sameAs locks the entity: it declares the business is the SAME entity as records at external URLs (citations, social profiles, Wikidata/KG), which is the mechanism Google uses to reconcile records into the Knowledge Graph. This is the buildable on-site component that most directly 'locks the entity' — but it is an entity-CLARITY/disambiguation signal, NOT a ranking multiplier. Honest framing: it helps Google be confident WHICH business you are, not rank you higher per se.
allClaims.stat: sameAs = entity reconciliation / Knowledge Graph identity link
allClaims.snippet: sameAs is used to declare that the subject of the schema (Person, Organization, Brand, etc.) is the same as another entity described at an external URL ... it facilitates Google's Knowledge Graph reconciliation ... improving entity recognition rather than acting as a direct ranking signal.

allClaims.claim: Independent 85-day controlled experiment (11 test pages vs 4 control) on place-based entity linking — using spatialCoverage/audience plus sameAs to link locations to Wikipedia/Wikidata/Google KG — produced a 46% increase in impressions and 42% increase in clicks for non-branded location queries. This is the strongest MEASURED corroboration that on-site geo entity-linking moves location-query VISIBILITY (organic impressions/clicks), and it is the buildable, config-driven payoff of the schema layer. Note: it measures organic location-query visibility, not local-pack position.
allClaims.stat: +46% impressions, +42% clicks (non-branded location queries), 85 days, 11 test / 4 control pages
allClaims.snippet: After running the experiment for 85 days, the test sites saw an increase in the number of queries containing the state name and 'near me', leading to a 46% increase in impressions and a 42% increase in clicks for non-branded queries.

allClaims.claim: Sterling Sky's controlled test found the URL you link from the Google Business Profile DOES impact local-pack ranking for the queries that page targets — moving a listing's link from the homepage to a niche service page improved visibility for those queries. This validates the GBP-link->dedicated-landing pattern as the buildable anti-cannibalization lever. CRITICAL HONESTY CAVEAT: their default recommendation for a SINGLE-location business is still the homepage (higher authority); dedicated city/service pages are the right call for multi-listing/practitioner cases OR when the homepage already ranks (post-2025 Diversity Update, linking the top-ranking page can HURT).
allClaims.stat: GBP landing-page URL content impacts pack ranking for that page's queries (measured)
allClaims.snippet: The content on the specific URL you link to is important and impacts ranking in the local results. ... [Feb 2025 update] linking to the highest-ranking organic page can now hurt rankings due to Google's Diversity Update, so they now recommend linking to relevant pages that aren't already ranking organically.

allClaims.claim: Sterling Sky's GBP landing-page guidance: multi-location/service-area businesses NEED a dedicated city page or city-specific service page per GBP location, and the landing page should mention all services so Google can trigger 'website mentions' justifications in the profile. This is the buildable spec: one dedicated, NAP-matched, service-listing landing page per location entity — exactly the config-driven locationNode + city-page pattern.
allClaims.stat: 1 dedicated city/service landing page per GBP location
allClaims.snippet: you will need a dedicated city page or a city-specific service page for each GBP location ... All services should be mentioned on the landing page to help Google understand offerings and trigger 'website mentions' justifications in the profile.

allClaims.claim: Sterling Sky's 8,186-business / 200-city near-me study found a (slight, directional) positive correlation between MORE SUBSTANTIVE WORDS on the linked landing page and better local rankings — i.e., thin location pages underperform deeper ones. This is independent, large-N evidence that the on-site content depth of the GBP landing page is a (modest) pack lever, and it reinforces the anti-doorway 'deep real content per location' build rule over thin city pages.
allClaims.stat: 8,186 businesses / 200 cities; 'slight correlation' between substantive page words and rankings
allClaims.snippet: a slight correlation between having more substantive words on your page and better local rankings ... 'Is Service Area Business' showed a negative correlation to ranking [hiding address hurts].

allClaims.claim: Embedding a Google Map / driving-directions on the site is a UX + trust + local-relevance reinforcement signal, NOT a standalone ranking factor — and after Google's 2018 crackdown, mass map-embedded geo pages became counterproductive/risky, plus heavy embeds can slow the page (page speed IS a ranking factor). Honest build rule: embed a real map on the contact/location page for trust and NAP confirmation, lazy-load it for CWV, and do NOT spin up hundreds of map-embed location pages expecting a ranking lift.
allClaims.stat: map embed = trust/UX, not a direct ranking factor; mass geo-embeds risky post-2018
allClaims.snippet: Yes, if you use it on your 'contact' or 'about us' page or similar. No, if you're creating a massive number of pages that have different Google Map locations on them. ... [Google] discontinued this practice [after SEOs created thousands of geo-targeted pages].

allClaims.claim: NAP consistency feeds the pack indirectly through the citation-signal cluster (citations ~11% of pack weight in current LSRF-style breakdowns), and consistency matters MORE than raw citation volume — a smaller set of perfectly consistent citations outperforms a larger inconsistent set. Buildable spec: a single config-driven NAP source-of-truth rendered identically in schema (PostalAddress/telephone), footer, and contact page so on-site NAP exactly matches the GBP and every citation. HONESTY FLAG: the popular '40% lift' / '156% Maps visibility' / '27% drop' figures circulate via vendor/agency blogs without a traceable primary study — treat as directional vendor claims, not measured fact.
allClaims.stat: citations ~11% pack weight; consistency > volume (vendor '40%/156%/27%' figures unverified)
allClaims.snippet: NAP consistency across the web is a signal Google uses to verify a business is legitimate and trustworthy; inconsistent NAP can confuse search engines and harm local rankings. [The specific 40%/156%/27% figures appear only on agency blogs without a traceable primary study.]

allClaims.claim: Entity resolution is a GATEKEEPING layer that runs BEFORE content retrieval/ranking in both classic and AI/LLM retrieval — a brand that fails entity recognition is excluded before passage scoring begins. This reframes the sameAs/NAP/@graph layer as a PREREQUISITE for eligibility (in the pack, organic, and AI citations), not a ranking boost. Directional and partly modeled, but it is the most honest 'why build the entity layer' argument: it's table-stakes to be in the consideration set, especially as AI-cited URLs increasingly fall outside the organic top-10.
allClaims.stat: entity resolution precedes ranking; ~77% of AI-cited URLs were outside organic top-10 (single study)
allClaims.snippet: Entity resolution runs before content retrieval: brands that fail it are excluded before passage scoring begins. ... 76.95% of AI-cited URLs were outside the organic top-10.

allClaims.claim: Using @id within the @graph (a single connected JSON-LD graph where LocalBusiness, location nodes, services, and breadcrumbs reference each other by @id) is the structural best practice for making entities machine-reconcilable for SEO, LLMs, and the Knowledge Graph. This validates the Summit & Oak architecture (already shipping @graph + locationNode) as the correct, config-driven entity-locking pattern rather than disconnected per-page snippets.
allClaims.stat: @id + @graph = connected-entity best practice for KG/LLM reconciliation
allClaims.snippet: Using @id in Schema.org markup creates persistent, referenceable entities so search engines and LLMs can connect and reconcile the same entity across a site and the wider web (Knowledge Graph).

allClaims.claim: LocalBusiness schema should carry geo (latitude/longitude), areaServed, and address (PostalAddress) so the markup explicitly states the served geography — the structured equivalent of the geo-grid the pack measures. This is config-driven from the same GEOGRAPHY block that drives the city pages, making service-area geo declaration a single source of truth across schema, copy, and the footer NAP.
allClaims.stat: LocalBusiness: geo + areaServed + PostalAddress declare served geography
allClaims.snippet: LocalBusiness ... properties include address (PostalAddress), geo (GeoCoordinates: latitude/longitude), and areaServed (the geographic area where a service or offered item is provided).

allClaims.claim: In Whitespark's 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors study, on-page/website signals account for roughly 19% of local-pack ranking weight — the third controllable lever after Google Business Profile (~32%) and review signals — confirming the on-site layer is real but minority-weighted in the PACK specifically.
allClaims.stat: On-page SEO ~19% of local-pack weight; GBP ~32%; reviews ~16-20%; behavioral ~8-9%; proximity ~55%
allClaims.snippet: On-page SEO accounts for roughly 19% of local ranking weight ... the most impactful element as LocalBusiness schema markup, location-specific title tags, and a fast mobile experience.

allClaims.claim: Whitespark's 2026 study ranks 'Dedicated Page for Each Service' as the #1 factor in Local Organic and #2 in AI Visibility — the single strongest endorsement that a config-driven service×city page architecture (exactly what we build) is the top on-site organic lever, distinct from the pack. This is the buildable component ranked #1.
allClaims.stat: Dedicated Page for Each Service = #1 Local Organic, #2 AI Visibility
allClaims.snippet: "Dedicated Page for Each Service" is cited as "#1 in Local Organic and #2 in AI Visibility" ... Site factors have gained prominence in both organic search and AI search.

allClaims.claim: For AI Search Visibility, on-page/website signals carry ~24% weight — HIGHER than for the local pack and, per the reporting, higher than GBP for AI — meaning the deep on-site authority layer we build is the PRIMARY lever for the emerging AI-citation surface, not a minority one. This is the forward-looking spine: organic/on-site depth wins the AI surface the pack can't reach.
allClaims.stat: On-page ~24% for AI Visibility (vs ~19% for local pack); website more important than GBP for AI
allClaims.snippet: for AI Search Visibility, on-page signals account for 24% (higher than the Local Pack), indicating that for AI visibility, the website is more important than the GBP.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: modeled (expert-survey weighting, Whitespark 2026); note: this exact 24% figure was reported via a search-engine snippet of koanthic.com which returned 403 on direct fetch — corroborate against the Whitespark primary before reel-binding

allClaims.claim: COUNTER-EVIDENCE / honesty anchor: Google's John Mueller has repeatedly confirmed schema/structured data is NOT a direct ranking factor — 'Using schema doesn't give you a ranking boost'; for local business he called it 'a very very small thing' for ranking. The on-site schema layer earns eligibility and entity-clarity, NOT a rank multiplier. Never sell schema as 'ranks you higher.'
allClaims.stat: Schema = not a ranking factor; 'very very small thing' for local ranking
allClaims.snippet: Mueller stated: "Using schema doesn't give you a ranking boost" ... structured data is not really something that would change the ranking of a page ... a "very very small thing" when it comes to ranking factors.

allClaims.claim: Reconciler for the AI-citation thesis: at Search Central Live Madrid (April 9-10, 2025) Google/Mueller reaffirmed it still RECOMMENDS structured data in an AI-search world because it lets machines 'read and index content more efficiently' — but framed it as supporting SERP-visible features, NOT a confirmed AI-ranking mechanism. Honest framing: schema makes the entity machine-legible (a crutch/clarifier), it does not 'cure' weak content or guarantee an AI citation.
allClaims.stat: Google reaffirmed structured data recommendation in AI-search era, April 2025
allClaims.snippet: Google still recommends to use structured data in an AI search world – focusing on those things that are actually visible in SERPs ... structured data enables computers to read and index content more efficiently. The article does not contain explicit statements confirming that Google uses structured data to power AI features or Gemini.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: directional (Google first-party, with explicit no-overclaim note)

allClaims.claim: Mueller's nuance on schema + LLMs: whether schema helps an LLM understand an entity 'depends' on the feature; some features lean heavily on structured data, others can be read from page text — and crucially schema 'cannot make a product rank higher or be named the best by AI systems.' Strongest honest line: schema is a machine-readability accelerant for entity understanding, not an AI-ranking lever.
allClaims.stat: Schema-helps-LLMs = 'it depends'; cannot make AI name you 'best'
allClaims.snippet: whether extensive schema markup helps LLMs understand entities better "depends" ... it's much easier for machines to read machine-readable data ... it cannot make a product rank higher or be named the "best" by AI systems.

allClaims.claim: Roofing-vertical MEASURED corroboration: a multi-location roofing contractor that rebuilt the site with a dedicated SEO-optimized page per office location + unique service pages per office (anti-duplicate) + LocalBusiness schema + NAP standardization saw organic traffic rise from 4.5K to 13K monthly (188%), ranking keywords +62.5% (4,000→6,500), and GBP calls/leads +145% (~988/mo). Directional vendor case study, but the work described maps 1:1 to our config-driven location-node + service-page build.
allClaims.stat: Roofing: organic +188% (4.5K→13K/mo), keywords +62.5%, GBP leads +145%
allClaims.snippet: Organic traffic increased from 4.5K to 13K monthly visitors, a 188% growth ... Ranking keywords increased from 4,000 to 6,500, a 62.5% growth ... Calls and leads from GBP increased by 145%, reaching about 988 monthly ... unique service pages developed under each office location to prevent duplicate content.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: measured-but-vendor-attributed (no isolated controlled variable; agency case study)

allClaims.claim: Defines the BLOCKING build rule for location pages (anti-doorway): a page crosses into doorway/spam when it is 'swapping city names across boilerplate copy' with 'no local proof' (no addresses, testimonials, or local context) and is orphaned from navigation — such pages land in 'Crawled – currently not indexed' and 'may rank lower in results or not appear in results at all.' Legitimacy requires localized content, service-area transparency, internal linking, and conversion intent. This is the spec our real-job→page gate enforces.
allClaims.stat: Doorway line = city-swapped boilerplate + no local proof + orphaned
allClaims.snippet: Swapping city names across boilerplate copy is duplication, not localization ... No local proof: claiming to serve an area without providing addresses, testimonials, or local context ... pages that live outside your site's navigation look disconnected, and Google sees them as lower quality ... Sites that violate our policies may rank lower in results or not appear in results at all.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: directional (restates Google doorway policy + GSC indexing behavior)

allClaims.claim: Independent large-scale recency 2025: across Google's 2024 March Core Update and 2025 updates, template-swapped location pages ('service in city A' / 'service in city B' using the same boilerplate) 'saw widespread demotions' under the Helpful Content System — so MORE thin city pages is a liability, reinforcing the depth-over-volume build rule (one deep real-job-backed page beats dozens of stamped ones).
allClaims.stat: Template-swapped city pages = 'widespread demotions' post-Mar-2024 core update
allClaims.snippet: Pages targeting minor keyword variants or replicating location templates, like "service in city A" and "service in city B," saw widespread demotions ... Google's Helpful Content System flags such content as unhelpful and may de-prioritize it for indexing.
allClaims.measured_or_modeled: directional (observed-pattern reporting, not a controlled study)

allClaims.claim: On-site review/testimonial display is justified by consumer behavior, not just ranking: 87% of consumers read online reviews for local businesses and only 4% 'never' do; 95% are more likely to trust a business with many reviews; 88% want multiple perspectives across platforms. Surfacing real, location-tagged reviews/testimonials on the site (a buildable on-site local-proof component) directly serves the conversion + local-relevance layer.
allClaims.stat: 87% read reviews; 4% never; 95% trust high-volume; 88% want multi-platform perspectives
allClaims.snippet: 87% read online reviews for local businesses ... Just 4% of consumers say they 'never' read online business reviews ... 95% of consumers say they're more likely to trust a business with many reviews compared to one with only a few ... 88% of consumers want to see multiple perspectives across review platforms.

pillars.title: The review-acquisition machine
pillars.section:
## PILLAR L5 — The Review-Acquisition Machine

**Bottom line.** Reviews are the fastest controllable local-search lever, and the lever is VELOCITY — fresh reviews per month — not raw total. King Maker ships a compliant, single-path review funnel plus the physical artifacts (Google QR + place-ID link on trucks, invoices, door-hangers); the client runs the actual send. The mechanism's job is to clear the early review floor fast and then sustain a steady monthly drip into the organic-prominence and trust engine. It is a necessary, high-correlation input — not a deterministic ranking dial.

**The spine: velocity, not volume.** Review recency moved to a top-5 local ranking factor in 2025, up from #20 in 2023 ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/blog/the-most-underrated-local-ranking-factor-in-2025/)); a business earning ~20 fresh reviews/month outranks one sitting on 200 reviews from two years ago ([whitespark.ca](https://whitespark.ca/local-search-ranking-factors/)). Rankings "fall off a cliff" when collection stops — an 18-day pause did it in Sterling Sky's 8,186-business / 200-city study, and recovery follows resumption ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/number-of-reviews-impact-ranking/)). That is the whole argument for a machine that produces a continuous drip rather than a one-time backfill. The early floor matters too: crossing 9→10 reviews produced a small ranking bump in all 3 test cases, with diminishing returns after ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/number-of-reviews-impact-ranking/)) — so clear the low roofing bar quickly, then let recency carry the weight.

**Compliance is a build constraint, not a config option.** Review GATING (happy customers get the Google link, unhappy ones get a private form) violates Google's UGC policy: businesses must not selectively solicit positive reviews or discourage negative ones ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114?hl=en)). It is also federal-law exposure — the FTC's final Rule on Consumer Reviews (effective Oct 21, 2024) bans review suppression and sentiment-incentivized reviews, with civil penalties up to ~$51,744 per violation ([alston.com](https://www.alston.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/ftc-issues-final-rule-on-fake-reviews-testimonials)). Many off-the-shelf "review funnels" sold to contractors ARE gating tools, so the KM funnel must be single-path and unscreened BY DESIGN — every customer gets the same Google link, no incentive. Genuine, unincentivized solicitation is explicitly permitted ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114?hl=en)); the machine operates inside that green light. Route the /review path to Google's own first-party shareable link + QR code, not a third-party intermediary ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/business/answer/16816815?hl=en)).

**Site-side reviews are content, not stars.** Self-hosted reviews on the reviewed entity's own site are INELIGIBLE for Google star rich-results under LocalBusiness or any Organization type — whether marked up directly or via an embedded Google/Facebook widget ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/review-snippet)); BrightLocal corroborates and points to Product/Service-scoped schema as the eligible path ([brightlocal.com](https://www.brightlocal.com/learn/review-schema/)). So a whole-company site-side aggregateRating will NOT render stars in search. Ship it as on-page content, E-E-A-T, and an AI-answer/entity signal — and reserve "star results" talk for Product/Service schema where genuinely applicable. Selling site reviews as "Google stars" is both ineffective and an FTC deceptive-claim risk.

**The request flow (client-run).** SMS out-opens email and converts better; fire within 24–48h of job completion, two sentences plus the link, personalized, with a single reminder at 3–5 days (more damages the relationship) ([wiserreview.com](https://wiserreview.com/blog/review-request-message/)). Point-of-job physical asks (QR/NFC cards, truck and invoice decals) lift volume at peak satisfaction. The conversion multipliers — ~98% SMS open vs ~20–30% email, 12–20% vs 3–8% completion, "3–5x" from cards — come from review-platform vendors who profit from the claim and rarely publish methodology ([birdeye.com](https://birdeye.com/blog/sms-vs-email-review-requests-2025/), [wiserreview.com](https://wiserreview.com/blog/google-review-card/)). Promise the floor (SMS reliably out-opens email; point-of-job physical asks raise volume); label the headline multipliers vendor-reported/directional.

**Scope, equity, cost, impact.** ONE-TIME / shippable: the single-path funnel build, the /review page wired to Google's place-ID link, the QR/NFC artifact set, and Product/Service review schema where applicable. ONGOING send cadence is the client's to run — out of scope here. Equity: reviews are a CITATION/trust/entity signal, not a backlink — there is no dofollow vs nofollow link-equity dimension to this lever (no PBNs, no link schemes, none of it touches this pillar). Approximate one-time cost: low — funnel + schema + artifact design is a small build line, the cost sits in the client's ongoing labor to ask. Impact-vs-effort: HIGH impact / LOW one-time effort — it is the cheapest, fastest-moving controllable signal, which is exactly why it anchors the offer.

**What NOT to oversell:** reviews are ~16–20% of pack weight while proximity (~55%) dominates ([sterlingsky.ca](https://www.sterlingsky.ca/number-of-reviews-impact-ranking/)) — this lever moves a heavily-correlated signal toward organic prominence and conversion; it does not buy a top-3 pack spot, and the pack stays a proximity-capped byproduct we never headline.

loadBearing.claim: Review recency/velocity is a top-5 local ranking factor in 2025 (up from #20 in 2023); ~20 fresh reviews/month outranks 200 stale ones — the machine must produce a steady monthly drip, not a one-time backfill.
loadBearing.stat: recency = top-5 factor 2025 (was #20 in 2023); 20 fresh/month beats 200 stale
loadBearing.snippet: In the 2023 Local Search Ranking Factors, Review Recency ranks as the #20th most valuable local ranking factor... I'd put review recency in my top 5 most important ranking factors of 2025.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: This is the spine of the entire pillar and the offer's velocity-machine logic. If recency weren't a top lever, the 'steady drip' mechanism wouldn't justify the offer headline. Independent (Whitespark/Darren Shaw) — strongest non-vendor endorsement.
loadBearing.measured_or_modeled: directional (named-expert assessment + practitioner survey consensus, Whitespark LSRF)

loadBearing.claim: Maps rankings 'fall off a cliff' when review collection stops (an 18-day pause did it in a 8,186-business / 200-city study) and recover when collection resumes — proving the value is sustained velocity, not a backfill.
loadBearing.stat: 8,186 businesses / 200 cities; ~18-day pause = ranking cliff
loadBearing.snippet: Rankings can 'fall off a cliff' if you stop receiving reviews for even three weeks... a dental client pulling 60+ reviews/month dominated, but rankings fell off during an 18-day pause.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Directly justifies an ONGOING drip over a one-time spike — the load-bearing distinction between KM's continuous machine and a backfill. Larger-N independent corroborator; correlation not proven causation, so frame as probable.
loadBearing.measured_or_modeled: measured (case-study observational, correlational; larger-N near-me study)

loadBearing.claim: Review gating (selectively soliciting positive reviews / screening out unhappy customers) violates Google's UGC policy AND the FTC's final review rule (effective Oct 21, 2024), with civil penalties up to ~$51,744 per violation — so the KM funnel must be single-path and unscreened by design.
loadBearing.stat: up to $51,744 per violation; FTC rule effective Oct 21, 2024; Google policy prohibition
loadBearing.source_type: legal-analysis (law firm citing FTC final rule)
loadBearing.snippet: The rule went into effect on October 21, 2024... gives the FTC authority to pursue significant monetary penalties... currently $51,744 per violation... a business cannot provide compensation to its customers for making a positive review.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: The FTC-exposure rail. Many contractor 'review funnels' on the market ARE gating tools; shipping one would be a compliance violation for KM. This is the build constraint that protects the offer from legal risk — pair with Google policy URL on the slide.
loadBearing.measured_or_modeled: measured (rule text + statutory penalty + Google policy text)

loadBearing.claim: Self-hosted reviews on the reviewed entity's own site are ineligible for Google star rich-results under LocalBusiness/Organization schema (directly or via embedded Google/Facebook widgets) — ship site-side reviews as content/E-E-A-T/AI-entity signal, not 'star results.'
loadBearing.stat: 0 star rich-results from self-hosted LocalBusiness reviews; Product/Service schema = eligible path
loadBearing.snippet: If the entity being reviewed controls the reviews about itself, their pages that use LocalBusiness or any other type of Organization structured data are ineligible for star review feature... either directly in their structured data or through an embedded third-party widget.
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Prevents an FTC-style deceptive-claim if KM sold site reviews as 'Google stars.' Defines what we CAN promise (content/AI signal) vs cannot (star SERP results). Google first-party doc — unimpeachable.

loadBearing.claim: Crossing 9→10 reviews produced a small but measurable Maps ranking bump in all 3 test cases with diminishing returns after — confirming an early floor target the machine clears fast, while ongoing weight comes from velocity not raw total.
loadBearing.stat: 9→10 reviews = ranking bump in 3/3 cases; no bump 10→11
loadBearing.snippet: In all three cases, we saw a small but noticeable increase in their Maps ranking... when the businesses went from 9 to 10 reviews... We did not see the bump [moving from 10 to 11].
loadBearing.whyLoadBearing: Sets the early-floor target the offer can promise (clear the low roofing review bar fast) while explicitly capping raw-volume promises past it — the honest counterweight that keeps the pillar from overselling 'more reviews = more rank.' Note n=3, small effect.

whatNotToOversell: Do NOT sell reviews as a deterministic ranking dial — reviews are ~16-20% of pack weight while proximity (~55%) dominates; the lever is heavily correlated and consensus-backed, not proven-causal (Sterling Sky/SEL caution correlation; one plausible mechanism is indirect via engagement/CTR).
Do NOT promise a top-3 map-pack spot from reviews — the pack is proximity-capped; center the machine on organic regional dominance and conversion/trust where reviews carry full weight.

Do NOT assert the SMS/card multipliers (98% open, 12-20% completion, 3-5x volume) as measured — they are vendor-reported/directional; promise only the floor (SMS out-opens email; point-of-job physical asks raise volume).

Do NOT claim site-side aggregateRating produces Google star results — self-hosted LocalBusiness/Organization reviews are ineligible; reserve star-results talk for Product/Service schema where genuinely applicable.
Do NOT ship or imply a gated 'happy/unhappy fork' funnel — it violates Google policy and the FTC rule; the funnel is single-path and unscreened by design.
Do NOT promise an ever-climbing review TOTAL as the value — the measurable bump is the early floor (9->10) plus sustained recency; sell consistency/velocity, not a vanity count.
Do NOT frame reviews as a backlink/equity play — there is no dofollow/nofollow dimension; it is a citation/trust/entity signal, and no PBN or link-scheme tactics touch this lever.
gaps: No PRIMARY (non-vendor) measured study isolating the conversion lift of QR/NFC review cards or SMS-vs-email specifically for roofing/home-services; current figures are vendor-reported and should be labeled directional until an independent source is found.

The exact reviews-share of pack weight (~20%) traces to Whitespark's expert-survey LSRF (modeled, not behavioral/causal) — no independent causal experiment quantifies review velocity's marginal pack lift in dollars.

Google's own enforcement frequency/penalty for review gating (vs the FTC's stated $51,744/violation) is not publicly quantified — Google states the policy but not a monetary penalty, so the hard legal exposure rests on the FTC rule.

Whether Product/Service-scoped schema can legitimately carry star rich-results for a roofing contractor (vs being treated as self-serving) needs a build-time validation pass in Google's Rich Results Test, not just doctrine.

No NC/Triangle-specific (Raleigh/Durham/Charlotte) roofing review-count benchmark found; the 34,111-profile YDOP study is national. A local geo-grid pull would be needed to set a market-specific floor for a KM client.

No independent (non-vendor) measurement of post-job SMS vs email review-completion RATES; round 1's 12-20% SMS figures remain vendor-sourced. The DIRECTION (SMS converts higher) is well-supported but the exact completion % stays vendor-incentive.

The exact quantitative weight of self-published/site-side review CONTENT as an AI-answer/LLM-citation (GEO) entity signal is asserted directionally across sources but not independently measured; treat the AI-entity-signal value of on-page reviews as directional.

Whitespark's 2026 LSRF report body would not render via fetch (header-only); the velocity #93->#11 and ~20% weight figures are corroborated via independent secondaries citing it, but the exact report-page wording was not captured first-hand.

Fashion Nova $4.2M figure was captured via secondary attributing it to the FTC; the FTC's own Q&A page returned 403. Anchor is solid (well-documented public action) but the primary FTC press text was not directly quoted this pass.

counter.point: Reviews are only ~20% of pack weight (Whitespark LSRF, expert-survey/modeled) and the 'Magic 10' bump was small and n=3; the review machine is a high-velocity NECESSARY input but not sufficient to win the pack alone — proximity, primary GBP category, and prominence co-determine ranking.
counter.soWhat: Sell the review machine as the fastest controllable lever and a velocity engine, not as a standalone ranking guarantee. Pair the offer's rank language with organic-prominence work, per the spine.

counter.point: The SMS-vs-email conversion multipliers (98% open, 12-20% completion, 3-5x volume from cards) come overwhelmingly from review-platform VENDORS who profit from the claim; the underlying field studies are rarely published with methodology. Independent corroboration is thin.
counter.soWhat: Promise the FLOOR (SMS reliably out-opens email; point-of-job physical asks raise volume) and label the headline multipliers vendor-reported/directional in any reel or pitch — do not assert 3-5x as measured.

counter.point: Many off-the-shelf 'review funnels' marketed to contractors are themselves gating tools (the happy-path/unhappy-path split). Shipping a generic widget risks shipping a compliance violation.
